items.body:
美国将对日本等14个国家和地区加征关税

11月25日，美国贸易代表办公室宣布，根据贸易法第301条，将对包括日本在内的14个国家和地区加征新的关税，理由是这些国家和地区过度生产和出口产品，给美国产业造成了损失。

其中关于日本，美国贸易代表办公室表示，经依法调查，认定日本对汽车、钢铁和半导体等行业的财政支持等导致商品的过度生产和出口，从而打击了美国产业。

加上已被征收的关税税率，来自日本的进口商品的关税税率最高将达到15%。

本次关税措施的实施日期尚未确定，预计明年1月下旬有关方面就此政策举行听证会后，新的关税就将开始加征。

关于特朗普政府实施的关税措施，今年7月，美国对60个国家和地区加征了新的关税，理由是上述国家和地区针对强迫劳动生产的产品未采取限制进口等措施。包括已被征收的税率在内，来自日本的进口商品的关税税率已达到12.5%。

而依照本次的新政策，包括上述税率在内，日本输美商品的关税税率最高将达到15%，这符合去年日美两国政府达成的协议。

items.body:
日本拟引进新型反舰导弹作为反击手段

相关人士25日透露，围绕日本政府计划年底修改的三份安全保障相关文件，其中《防卫力整备计划》的指针写明，作为反击能力（对敌基地攻击能力）手段的长射程导弹，将引进可由自卫队舰艇发射的新型反舰导弹。此外也包括着眼于突发事态之际的紧急增产，将在所有领域推进装备品国产化。考虑到招募困难和少子化影响，还将重新审视陆上自卫队的组织架构和人员定额。

　　下一期整备计划将规定拟采购的主要装备以及2027至2031年度的防卫费总额。日本政府正在推进对防卫省估算的70万亿至80多万亿日元进行大幅压缩。不过，根据政府内部协调情况，采购规模仍有可能发生变化。

　　新型反舰导弹计划搭载在类似运输集装箱的箱式发射装置上，并考虑使其具有在多种舰艇上展开运用的功能。在太空领域，将部署中轨道常态监视系统，以持续监控广域范围，提升对敌方舰艇的探测能力等，从而增强反击能力的实效性。

　　针对中国和俄罗斯正在推进研发、用于攻击他国卫星的所谓“杀手卫星”，日本将配备用于保护本国卫星的“保镖卫星”。此外还将采购可用于救援和发射导弹的中型无人水面艇。

　　由于自卫官长期存在人员缺额的问题，不仅是陆自，海上自卫队也将推进无人化，以提高舰艇和飞机运用体制的效率。航空自卫队被写明将重组战机部队。

　　为维持必要战力，将力争延长飞机和舰艇的服役运用年限。同时也将强化保护关键基础设施在平时到突发事态的所有阶段免受网络攻击的防卫能力。对人工智能（AI）运用的定位是“对与美国开展联合行动而言也不可或缺”，并提出将为推动AI相关事业发展进行重点投资。

items.title: 纽约时报双语版
items.summary: 研究称立场亲北京的AI虚假账号试图影响台湾选情 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
JULIAN E. BARNES2026年11月26日

2024年台湾总统选举期间，台北的投票点。台湾将于11月28日举行地方选举。 Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times

Researchers have discovered a coordinated social media campaign powered by artificial intelligence that appears to be trying to influence elections in Taiwan this month.

研究人员发现，一场由人工智能驱动的协同社交媒体行动似乎正试图影响台湾本月的选举。

Fake accounts believed to be controlled by groups aligned with China’s government are pushing messages that support the policies and positions of the Chinese Communist Party.

据信由与中国政府立场一致的团体控制的虚假账号正在推送支持中国共产党政策与立场的信息。

China’s information operations have traditionally lacked sophistication, according to U.S. former officials and experts. But the research suggests that China has used A.I. — and possibly studied Russian efforts — to improve its methods.

美国前官员和专家表示，中国的信息战行动传统上较为简陋。但这项研究表明，中国已利用人工智能——并可能借鉴了俄罗斯的做法——来改进其手段。

Taiwan is holding local elections on Nov. 28 to fill more than 11,000 offices in cities and counties across the island. China considers Taiwan, a self-governed democracy, as part of its territory.

台湾将于11月28日举行地方选举，选出全岛各县市11000多个公职人员。中国将实行自治民主制度的台湾视为其领土的一部分。

The National Security Bureau, Taiwan’s civilian intelligence agency, has warned about Chinese interference in the election. And Taiwanese officials this month flagged to Meta thousands of accounts that they said were linked to China and were involved in the campaign.

台湾民事情报机构“国家安全局”已就中国干预此次选举发出警告。台湾官员本月也向Meta标记了数千个账号，称这些账号与中国有关联且参与了此次行动。

In October and November, researchers at Vanderbilt University observed “traditional, hybrid and A.I.-powered inauthentic activity” aimed at influencing the vote, according to the research report.

研究报告显示，10月和11月，范德堡大学的研究人员观察到旨在影响投票的“传统、混合以及人工智能驱动的非真实活动”。

Last year, Vanderbilt researchers uncovered an effort by GoLaxy, a Chinese company, to develop artificial intelligence tools to create sophisticated disinformation campaigns. Working with Doublethink Lab, a nonprofit organization in Taiwan, the researchers began searching for evidence of China’s expanding A.I.-powered influence operations.

去年，范德堡大学的研究人员发现，中国企业中科天玑正试图开发人工智能工具，以制造复杂的虚假信息行动。研究人员与台湾非营利组织台湾民主实验室合作，开始寻找中国不断扩大的人工智能驱动影响力行动的证据。

The research uses a new tool developed by the Vanderbilt lab to detect A.I.-generated posts and other inauthentic material in both English and Chinese.

这项研究使用范德堡大学实验室开发的一种新工具，检测英文和中文的人工智能生成帖文及其他非真实内容。

The research team “developed methods to find subtle differences between human and A.I. operators’ tone and word preferences,” said Brett J. Goldstein, the director of the Wicked Problems Lab at Vanderbilt’s Institute of National Security. “This let us identify patterns across seemingly unrelated accounts that were peddling political narratives.”

范德堡大学国家安全研究所棘手问题实验室主任布雷特·J·戈德斯坦表示，研究团队“开发了识别人类与人工智能操作者在语气和用词偏好上细微差异的方法”。“这使我们能够在看似互不关联、却都在兜售政治叙事的账号之间识别出规律。”

The tool and the researchers found inauthentic accounts aligned with Beijing that were either posting on nonpolitical topics, like food, animals or celebrities, or creating social media feeds featuring sexualized imagery, known as “thirst traps.” Interspersed in those otherwise entertainment-oriented feeds were messages supporting China or unification.

该工具和研究人员发现，与北京立场一致的非真实账号要么发布美食、动物或名人等非政治话题，要么创建包含性感挑逗图像的社交媒体动态，即所谓的“诱惑陷阱”。在这些原本以娱乐为主的动态中，穿插着支持中国或统一的信息。

Some of the accounts posted material directly attacking the Democratic Progressive Party, Taiwan’s governing party, accusing it of corruption or criticizing its record in office.

部分账号发布内容直接攻击台湾执政党民进党，指责其腐败或批评其施政表现。

Other fake accounts took a more sophisticated approach. One presented itself as supporting the governing party. But that inauthentic account responded to pro-Chinese accounts that were not gaining traction to give Beijing’s messaging more attention, the Vanderbilt researchers found.

还有一些虚假账号则采取了更为老练的手法。范德堡大学研究人员发现，有一个账号将自己包装成支持执政党的形象，却会回复那些未能引起关注的亲中账号，以使北京方面的信息获得更多关注。

Accounts across platforms coordinate messaging and appear to be testing different strategies, the research found.

研究发现，跨平台的账号在信息发布上相互协调，且似乎正在测试不同的策略。

Spokespeople for the Chinese Embassy and Taiwan’s office in Washington did not respond to requests for comment.

中国驻美大使馆和台湾驻华盛顿代表处的发言人均未回应置评请求。

The technique of putting political messages in unrelated, celebrity-focused feeds was observed during the U.S. midterm elections. Alethea, a threat intelligence company, identified the fake accounts, which were aiming to undermine Democrats, as being Russian in origin.

在无关的、以名人为中心的动态中植入政治信息的手法，在美国中期选举期间也曾被观察到。威胁情报公司Alethea认定，那些旨在削弱民主党人的虚假账号源自俄罗斯。

The Vanderbilt research showed that accounts spent months posting provocative A.I.-generated images on Instagram, and then added political content on Threads, a companion social media platform, as Taiwan’s election approached.

范德堡大学的研究显示，一些账号花了数月时间在Instagram上发布挑逗性的人工智能生成图像，随后在台湾选举临近之际，在配套社交媒体平台Threads上加入了政治内容。

Brett Benson, a political science professor at Vanderbilt, said the new disinformation campaign in Taiwan showed a remarkable amount of patience.

范德堡大学政治学教授布雷特·本森表示，台湾此次出现的新型虚假信息行动展现出了惊人的耐心。

“Synthetic personas sometimes spend months posting nonpolitical content, cultivating followers and establishing an apparently authentic social media presence before introducing political messaging,” Mr. Benson said. “A.I. is making it easier to construct and maintain synthetic identities that can establish credibility within social networks before being mobilized for political purposes.”

“合成虚拟人设有时会花数月时间发布非政治内容，积累粉丝并建立看似真实的社交媒体形象，然后再引入政治信息，”本森说。“人工智能正使构建和维护合成身份变得更加容易，这些身份在被用于政治目的之前，就能在社交网络中建立起可信度。”

Many of the accounts tracked by the research appeared to be so-called cyborg accounts, which mix A.I.-generated imagery or slogans with the work of human propagandists. Some of the accounts posted during regular business hours, suggesting that people were involved in operating them and that they were not purely automated.

该研究追踪的许多账号似乎是所谓的“赛博格”账号，即将人工智能生成的图像或口号与人类宣传人员的工作相结合。部分账号在正常办公时间发帖，表明有人参与操作，并非纯粹自动化运作。

The earlier Vanderbilt research on GoLaxy revealed that the company was trying to use A.I. to create hyper-targeted messaging, hoping to craft large numbers of messages to persuade people based on their specific views.

范德堡大学此前针对中科天玑的研究显示，该公司曾试图利用人工智能制造超精准定向信息，希望根据人们的具体观点撰写大量信息以说服受众。

The new Vanderbilt program has not found evidence of such hyper-targeted campaigns, but researchers said they were continuing to look.

范德堡大学的这一新项目尚未发现此类超精准定向行动的证据，但研究人员表示他们仍在继续寻找。

Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。

翻译：纽约时报中文网

“合成虚拟人设有时会花数月时间发布非政治内容，积累粉丝并建立看似真实的社交媒体形象，然后再引入政治信息，”本森说。“人工智能正使构建和维护合成身份变得更加容易，这些身份在被用于政治目的之前，就能在社交网络中建立起可信度。”

Many of the accounts tracked by the research appeared to be so-called cyborg accounts, which mix A.I.-generated imagery or slogans with the work of human propagandists. Some of the accounts posted during regular business hours, suggesting that people were involved in operating them and that they were not purely automated.
该研究追踪的许多账号似乎是所谓的“赛博格”账号，即将人工智能生成的图像或口号与人类宣传人员的工作相结合。部分账号在正常办公时间发帖，表明有人参与操作，并非纯粹自动化运作。

The earlier Vanderbilt research on GoLaxy revealed that the company was trying to use A.I. to create hyper-targeted messaging, hoping to craft large numbers of messages to persuade people based on their specific views.
范德堡大学此前针对中科天玑的研究显示，该公司曾试图利用人工智能制造超精准定向信息，希望根据人们的具体观点撰写大量信息以说服受众。
The new Vanderbilt program has not found evidence of such hyper-targeted campaigns, but researchers said they were continuing to look.

items.body:
JULIAN E. BARNES, MAGGIE HABERMAN, JONATHAN SWAN2026年11月26日

2024年，英伟达的黄仁勋与黄乐在台北的一次聚会上。 via Reuters

A day after President Trump publicly proclaimed that Jensen Huang was not a national security threat or facing criminal prosecution, U.S. officials provided a tempered account of the intelligence at the heart of the Nvidia scandal in a briefing for Congress on Tuesday, people told about the briefing said.

据知情人士透露，在特朗普总统公开宣称黄仁勋不构成国家安全威胁，也不会面临刑事起诉的次日，美国官员在周二为国会举行的简报会上对英伟达丑闻核心的情报做出了较为克制的说明。

The briefing, for staff members of the House and Senate intelligence committees and aides to the leaders of both chambers, outlined in broad terms some of what intelligence agencies have collected on Alice Huang, the Chinese woman whose affair with the Nvidia chief is at the center of the episode.

此次简报会面向众议院和参议院情报委员会的工作人员以及两院领导人的助手，大体概述了情报机构收集到的有关黄乐(Alice Huang)的部分信息。这名中国女子与这位英伟达首席执行官的婚外情是此次事件的核心。

The U.S. intelligence officials told the aides to the lawmakers that they still do not fully understand the role played by Ms. Huang, who helped to run a Singapore-based data center firm, Megaspeed, that is suspected of diverting advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips to China.

美国情报官员告诉议员助手们，他们仍未完全弄清黄乐所扮演的角色。黄乐曾协助运营一家总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司Megaspeed，该公司涉嫌将先进的英伟达人工智能芯片转移到中国。

The briefers, who included officials from the F.B.I., C.I.A. and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, explained the contacts between Ms. Huang and China’s Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the meeting. The intelligence officials told the group there was no evidence she was directed by that agency to initiate an affair with Mr. Huang, though they did not dispute that she passed intelligence back to the agency after the affair began.

据听取了会议简报的人士称，包括来自联邦调查局、中央情报局和国家情报总监办公室官员在内的简报人员详细说明了黄乐与中国国家安全部之间的联系。情报官员告诉与会人员，没有证据表明她是受该机构指使才与黄仁勋发生婚外情的，但他们并未否认她在婚外情开始后向该机构传递了情报。

The briefers told the congressional staffers that the man who was often introduced as Ms. Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, was a more significant figure. He had been, at least at times, an M.S.S. asset and had more significant contacts with the Chinese spy agency, the briefers said.

简报人员告诉国会工作人员，经常被介绍为黄乐丈夫的男子康伟是一个更重要的人物。简报人员称，他至少在某些时候曾是中国国安部的线人，并且与这家中国间谍机构有着更密切的联系。

The briefing did not include the most sensitive intelligence that the U.S. has collected about Ms. Huang, nor did it include a highly classified March 30 memo overseen by Marco Rubio, the secretary of state and national security adviser. That memo described Mr. Huang’s relationship with Ms. Huang, and hers with Chinese intelligence services, according to people briefed on it.

此次简报并未包含美国收集到的有关黄乐的最敏感信息，也没有包括一份由国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥监督起草、于3月30日发布的高度机密备忘录。据知情人士透露，该备忘录描述了黄仁勋与黄乐的关系，以及黄乐与中国情报部门的关系。

The briefers, in a two-hour session, provided the senior congressional staff members with sensitive material that had been recently collected and with the information provided to senior intelligence officials, according to multiple people briefed of the session.

据多名听取了会议情况介绍的人士称，在长达两小时的会议中，简报人员向国会高级幕僚提供了近期收集的敏感材料，以及提供给高级情报官员的信息。

The congressional intelligence committees have requested a copy of the Rubio memo.

国会情报委员会已要求获取鲁比奥备忘录的副本。

The New York Times reported last month that the U.S. government had collected intelligence showing that Mr. Huang, an ally of Mr. Trump, was having a close relationship with Ms. Huang, who U.S. officials believed was an asset of Chinese intelligence services.

《纽约时报》上个月报道称，美国政府收集到的情报显示，特朗普盟友黄仁勋与黄乐关系密切，而美国官员认为黄乐是中国情报部门的线人。

The Times reported on Sunday that people briefed on the U.S. intelligence said Ms. Huang was in contact with the Chinese spy agency from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, covering at least part of the period when she was having the affair with Mr. Huang. The Times also reported that Mr. Kang was in contact with the spy agency, as well.

《纽约时报》周日报道称，知情人士透露，黄乐从2025年春季到今年秋季一直与中国间谍机构保持联系，这至少涵盖了她与黄仁勋保持婚外情的部分时期。《纽约时报》还报道称，康伟也与该间谍机构有联系。

Soon after The Times first reported last month on Ms. Huang’s links to Chinese intelligence, Mr. Trump publicly suggested that he was unsure whether Ms. Huang was a spy, and declared Mr. Huang a good man and a genius deserving of support from the government. Over this past weekend, the president set in motion a drive by the White House to reinstate Mr. Huang as Nvidia’s chief executive, reversing the Nvidia board’s decision to force his resignation.

上月《纽约时报》首次报道黄乐与中国情报部门的联系后不久，特朗普公开表示，他不确定黄乐是否是间谍，并宣称黄仁勋是个好人、是个天才，值得政府支持。在刚刚过去的这个周末，总统启动了一项由白宫主导的行动，旨在恢复黄仁勋作为英伟达首席执行官的职务，从而推翻了英伟达董事会迫使其辞职的决定。

The company’s announcement Monday that Mr. Huang would return was quickly followed by a social media statement from Mr. Trump in which the president asserted that the Nvidia chief was not a security threat and that he was not a target of any criminal prosecution. Mr. Trump made those statements even though he was briefed at least twice about Ms. Huang’s ties to Chinese intelligence, including once by Mr. Rubio, The Times has reported, and even though the Justice Department investigation into the diversion of chips to China is still in an early stage.

该公司周一宣布黄仁勋将回归后，特朗普紧接着在社交媒体上发表声明，坚称这位英伟达首席执行官不构成安全威胁，也不是任何刑事起诉的目标。据《纽约时报》报道，尽管特朗普至少听取过两次有关黄乐与中国情报部门联系的简报（其中一次由鲁比奥进行），且司法部对芯片转移至中国的调查仍处于早期阶段，但他仍发表了上述言论。

The briefing on Tuesday for congressional aides continued, behind closed doors, the public pattern by the administration of seeking to minimize any damage to Mr. Huang and Nvidia from the episode.

周二为国会助手举行的闭门简报会延续了政府此前公开表现的模式，即力图将此次事件对黄仁勋和英伟达造成的损害降至最低。

On Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche followed up on Mr. Trump’s statements, saying there was no evidence that Nvidia was anything other than “a good corporate citizen” and repeating that there was no evidence of wrongdoing by Mr. Huang.

周二，司法部长托德·布兰奇呼应了特朗普的声明，称没有证据表明英伟达不是“一家优秀的企业公民”，并重申没有证据表明黄仁勋有任何不当行为。

特朗普总统公开宣称，英伟达的黄仁勋既不构成国家安全威胁，也不面临刑事起诉。

In an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang had nothing to hide and that he should not invoke his Fifth Amendment right against self-incrimination during a scheduled hearing before Congress next week. Asked about issuing a pardon for Mr. Huang, Mr. Trump replied, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”

在周二接受《纽约邮报》采访时，特朗普表示，黄仁勋没有什么可隐瞒的，在下周国会举行的听证会上，他不应援引宪法第五修正案赋予的不自证其罪的权利。当被问及是否会赦免黄仁勋时，特朗普回答说：“我想这始终是一个选项，但我认为没有必要。”

Megaspeed, the data center company that employed Ms. Huang, is under investigation by the Justice Department for diverting advanced Nvidia chips to China to evade U.S. export controls. The Trump administration on Monday placed Megaspeed on a trading blacklist, meaning that U.S. companies cannot ship technology to Megaspeed without obtaining a license.

雇佣黄乐的数据中心公司Megaspeed目前正因涉嫌将先进的英伟达芯片转移至中国以规避美国出口管制而接受司法部的调查。特朗普政府周一将Megaspeed列入贸易黑名单，这意味着美国公司在未获得许可证的情况下不能向Megaspeed出口技术产品。

In restoring Mr. Huang to the chief executive role on Monday, Nvidia agreed to establish a chief compliance officer, in effect acknowledging that it needs to do more to police where its chips end up.

在周一恢复黄仁勋首席执行官职务的同时，英伟达同意设立首席合规官一职，这实际上承认了该公司需要采取更多措施来监管其芯片的最终流向。

In recent years the M.S.S., China’s top spy agency, has prioritized trying to break what Beijing calls an American “blockade” that is restricting their access to the most advanced computer chips.

近年来，中国最高间谍机构国家安全部将突破北京所称的美国“封锁”作为优先任务，该“封锁”限制了中国获取最先进计算机芯片的渠道。

The spy agency has worked to help Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into China. The M.S.S., according to U.S., European and Asian national security officials, also collects intelligence about the semiconductor sector and its supply chains.

该间谍机构一直致力于协助中国企业获取先进芯片并将其走私到中国。据美国、欧洲和亚洲的国家安全官员称，中国国安部还收集有关半导体行业及其供应链的情报。

Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。

Maggie Haberman是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。

Jonathan Swan是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统。

翻译：纽约时报中文网

雇佣黄乐的数据中心公司Megaspeed目前正因涉嫌将先进的英伟达芯片转移至中国以规避美国出口管制而接受司法部的调查。特朗普政府周一将Megaspeed列入贸易黑名单，这意味着美国公司在未获得许可证的情况下不能向Megaspeed出口技术产品。
In restoring Mr. Huang to the chief executive role on Monday, Nvidia agreed to establish a chief compliance officer, in effect acknowledging that it needs to do more to police where its chips end up.
在周一恢复黄仁勋首席执行官职务的同时，英伟达同意设立首席合规官一职，这实际上承认了该公司需要采取更多措施来监管其芯片的最终流向。
In recent years the M.S.S., China’s top spy agency, has prioritized trying to break what Beijing calls an American “blockade” that is restricting their access to the most advanced computer chips.
近年来，中国最高间谍机构国家安全部将突破北京所称的美国“封锁”作为优先任务，该“封锁”限制了中国获取最先进计算机芯片的渠道。

The spy agency has worked to help Chinese companies acquire and smuggle advanced chips into China. The M.S.S., according to U.S., European and Asian national security officials, also collects intelligence about the semiconductor sector and its supply chains.
该间谍机构一直致力于协助中国企业获取先进芯片并将其走私到中国。据美国、欧洲和亚洲的国家安全官员称，中国国安部还收集有关半导体行业及其供应链的情报。
Julian E. Barnes为《纽约时报》报道美国情报机构和国际安全事务。他撰写安全相关议题已有20余年。

items.body:
TONY ROMM, ANA SWANSON2026年11月26日

特朗普总统将第二次依据《1974年贸易法》第301条大规模征收关税。 The New York Times

The Trump administration proposed a slate of new tariffs on Wednesday targeting imports from dozens of countries, including China, Japan and the members of the European Union, marking the latest expansion of a global trade war that faces mounting obstacles in Congress and the courts.

特朗普政府周三提出了一系列新关税措施，针对来自数十个国家的进口商品，其中包括中国、日本和欧盟成员国。这标志着全球贸易战再升级，尽管这场贸易战在国会和法院面临越来越多的阻力。

The administration framed the duties as a response to unfair trade practices, as it accused some of its closest economic partners of overproducing certain products, undercutting American businesses and contributing to a swelling U.S. trade deficit.

政府将这些关税描绘为对不公平贸易行为的回应，并指责一些最亲密的经济伙伴过度生产某些产品，冲击美国企业，并导致美国贸易逆差不断扩大。

The newly unveiled roster of tariffs included a 20 percent tax on some imports from China, which the Trump administration signaled it could ratchet up — to 40 percent — if Beijing does not hew to the terms of a trade truce it has struck with Washington.

新公布的关税清单包括对部分中国进口商品征收20%的关税，特朗普政府表示，如果北京不遵守与华盛顿达成的贸易休战条款，可能将税率提高至40%。

The Trump administration also proposed similarly high and potentially escalating rates on goods from the 27 members of the European Union and other trading partners including Cambodia, India, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. Some of those duties could reach up to 20 percent as well. And it coupled the sweeping action with a separate, specific proposal seeking to raise rates on Brazil, targeting its sugar and aircraft exports.

特朗普政府还提议对欧盟27个成员国以及柬埔寨、印度、韩国、台湾和越南等其他贸易伙伴的商品征收类似的高税率，且可能进一步上调。其中一些关税也可能高达20%。与此同时，特朗普政府还单独提出了一项针对巴西的加税方案，目标是该国出口的糖和飞机。

Before the new tariffs take effect, the administration must fulfill a set of final regulatory requirements, which would include seeking public feedback, according to Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, who appeared Wednesday on CNBC. He described the approach as “targeted,” but noted that discussions continued with each of the affected trading partners.

美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔周三在接受CNBC采访时表示，在新关税生效之前，政府必须完成一系列最终监管要求，其中包括征求公众意见。他称这种做法是“具针对性的”，但指出，美国仍在与每个受影响的贸易伙伴进行磋商。

In many cases, though, Mr. Greer said the tariffs would not stack on top of those that the administration had already put in place. That included duties that President Trump has applied on national security grounds to products such as steel and cars. He said the White House also sought to keep its tariffs in line with the trade agreements it had already brokered.

不过，格里尔表示，在许多情况下，新关税不会与特朗普政府已经实施的关税叠加征收，其中包括特朗普总统以国家安全为由对钢铁和汽车等产品征收的关税。他说，白宫也力求确保其关税措施与已经达成的贸易协议保持一致。

The battery of new tariffs nonetheless arrived at a precarious political moment for Mr. Trump, who has continued to engage in a strategy of aggressive trade brinkmanship even after the Supreme Court struck down his initial slate of country-by-country duties this year.

然而，这一系列新关税措施出台之际，特朗普正处于政治上的艰难时刻。即便最高法院今年已裁定他最初推出的针对不同国家分别征收关税的措施无效，他仍继续推行激进的贸易边缘政策。

Mr. Trump has long portrayed tariffs as essential for boosting domestic manufacturing, raising revenue and fostering better trade deals. But his shifting policies have still counted among the many forces driving up prices for consumers and business, feeding a public backlash that ultimately stripped Republicans of their congressional majorities in the midterm election.

长期以来，特朗普一直宣称，关税对于振兴国内制造业、增加财政收入以及争取更有利的贸易协议至关重要。但他反复变化的政策仍是推高消费者和企业成本的诸多因素之一，由此引发的公众不满最终导致共和党在中期选举中失去了国会两院的多数席位。

Still, the White House risked touching off a widespread backlash — angering Congress, as Democrats prepare to take control of the House and the Senate, and rattling Wall Street, where stocks fell sharply to open trading on Wednesday. It coincided with the government’s release of a key gauge of inflation, which showed that prices rose 3.8 percent in October from a year earlier, marking a pickup from September.

尽管如此，白宫还是冒着引发广泛反弹的风险采取了这一行动——此举可能激怒即将由民主党掌控参众两院的国会，也令华尔街感到不安，周三股市开盘后大幅下挫。与此同时，政府公布了一项关键通胀指标，数据显示10月份物价同比上涨3.8%，涨幅较9月份有所加快。

The announcement also appeared to rankle the country’s closest allies and trading partners. Some had already struck deals with Mr. Trump to avert higher tariffs — or were in the midst of negotiations — when the administration signaled Wednesday that it could raise rates even higher.

这一宣布似乎也激怒了美国最亲密的盟友和贸易伙伴。其中一些已与特朗普达成协议，以避免被征收更高的关税，还有一些仍在谈判中，而特朗普政府周三却释放出可能进一步提高关税税率的信号。

In the European Union, officials said they would study the Trump administration’s findings but disputed that Europe was the source of overproduction. Olof Gill, a spokesperson for the bloc, said E.U. members expected “any measure from this investigation to respect” the trade deal between Brussels and Washington.

欧盟官员表示将研究特朗普政府的调查结果，但质疑欧洲是产能过剩源头的说法。欧盟发言人奥洛夫·吉尔表示，欧盟成员国希望美国“根据此次调查采取的任何措施”都能尊重布鲁塞尔与华盛顿之间的贸易协议。

Mr. Trump’s newly proposed tariffs on the European Union would be set at 15 percent, as the agreement between trans-Atlantic partners had stipulated. But the administration also warned it could raise rates as high as 25 percent if it found compliance was “unsatisfactory.”

按照跨大西洋贸易伙伴之间达成的协议，特朗普此次提议对欧盟征收的关税税率将定为15%。但特朗普政府同时警告，如果发现欧盟履行协议的情况“不尽如人意”，可能将税率提高至25%。

In China, meanwhile, officials also reacted forcefully to the White House’s latest tariff actions, just days after the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, hosted Mr. Trump for another round of trade talks. “The so-called overcapacity is a false proposition, and China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation,” said Guo Jiakun, spokesman for China’s foreign ministry.

与此同时，中国官员也对白宫最新的关税行动作出了强烈回应。就在几天前，中国领导人习近平刚刚接待特朗普，举行了新一轮贸易谈判。中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆表示：“所谓‘产能过剩’是一个伪命题，中方反对以此为借口进行政治操弄。”

The Trump administration said it would enforce the new duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which permits the U.S. government to investigate unfair trade practices abroad and impose tariffs in response to its findings. It is a power that presidents of both parties, including Mr. Trump, have invoked successfully in the past.

特朗普政府表示将根据1974年《贸易法》第301条执行新关税。该条款允许美国政府调查海外不公平贸易行为，并根据调查结果征收关税。过去，包括特朗普在内的两党总统都曾成功援引这一权力。

Under Section 301, the government can impose tariffs only after investigating and uncovering evidence that other countries discriminated or impeded U.S. industries. The administration announced two such inquiries in March, as it sought ways to resuscitate the tariffs that the Supreme Court had invalidated.

根据第301条，政府只有在调查并发现其他国家歧视或阻碍美国产业的证据后，才能征收关税。今年3月，为寻求恢复被最高法院裁定无效的关税措施，特朗普政府宣布启动两项此类调查。

One of those inquiries focused on dozens of countries for failing to crack down on forced labor. Those tariffs, which took effect in July, sparked a swift court challenge — and now await a verdict from a panel of judges that recently seemed poised to rule against the administration.

其中一项调查针对数十个未能有效打击强迫劳动的国家。由此产生的关税于7月生效，随即遭到法律挑战。目前，这些关税正等待一个法官合议庭作出裁决，而该合议庭最近似乎倾向于作出不利于特朗普政府的裁决。

The second investigation targeted what the administration has described as “excess capacity.” At the time, Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, said the inquiry would focus on the extent to which dozens of countries had unfairly boosted their manufacturing sectors and overproduced goods to the detriment of American industry.

第二项调查针对特朗普政府所称的“产能过剩”问题。美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔当时表示，调查将着重了解数十个国家在多大程度上以不公平的手段扶持本国制造业、过度生产商品，从而损害美国工业的利益。

On Mr. Greer’s radar was a wide range of foreign practices, including other countries’ use of state subsidies; their currency management; their support for state-owned enterprises; and their economic, labor and environmental regulations. For the administration, the main concern was that these practices gave foreign industry an unfair advantage over American manufacturers while driving up the nation’s trade deficit, which Mr. Trump has struggled to reduce.

格里尔关注的是外国采取的一系列做法，包括政府补贴、货币管理、对国有企业的扶持，以及经济、劳工和环境监管政策。特朗普政府主要担心的是，这些做法使外国工业相对于美国制造商获得了不公平的竞争优势，同时加剧了美国的贸易逆差，而特朗普一直未能有效缩减这一逆差。

This month, the government reported that the deficit reached $105 billion in September, a slight decrease from August yet still the second-largest total since Mr. Trump returned to office. A key force behind that imbalance is artificial intelligence, a priority for Mr. Trump, as U.S. firms snap up expensive semiconductors and other computing components from abroad.

本月，美国政府公布的数据显示，9月份贸易逆差达到1050亿美元，较8月份略有下降，但仍是特朗普重返白宫以来第二高的水平。造成这一贸易失衡的一个重要因素是人工智能，而这恰恰是特朗普的优先事项，因为美国企业正在从海外大量采购价格高昂的半导体及其他计算机零部件。

Some business owners criticized the tariffs, saying that Americans were already struggling with affordability concerns and that new tariffs could force them to raise prices again.

一些企业主对新关税提出批评，称美国民众已经在为生活成本问题苦苦挣扎，而新关税可能迫使企业再次提高价格。

Anne-Marie De Witt, the chief executive of Fireside Games, a board game publisher in Austin, Texas, said the move was “especially disheartening after the electorate spoke extremely clearly about the hardship tariffs are placing on the budgets of all Americans.”

总部位于得克萨斯州奥斯汀的桌游发行商Fireside Games的首席执行官安妮-玛丽·德维特表示，此举“尤其令人沮丧，选民已经非常明确地表达了关税给所有美国人的生计造成的困难”。

She issued the criticism alongside We Pay the Tariffs, a coalition of small businesses that has fought Mr. Trump’s trade policies. In response to the announcement on Wednesday, Ms. De Witt added, “We have all suffered enough.”

她与一直反对特朗普贸易政策的小企业联盟“关税由我们埋单”共同提出了这一批评。针对周三公布的关税措施，德维特还说：“我们受的苦已经够多了。”

Other groups welcomed the move. In a release, the United Steelworkers union called the crackdown “long overdue" and said that extended global dialogues in recent years had failed to make progress on excess capacity in a range of industries, from steel and aluminum to chemicals, tires and ships.

其他团体则欢迎这一举措。美国钢铁工人联合会在新闻稿中称此次打击“早该进行”，并表示近年来旷日持久的全球对话未能在钢铁、铝、化工、轮胎和船舶等一系列行业的产能过剩问题上取得进展。

“America’s manufacturing workers have been under attack for far too long, and now we have an opportunity to start restoring fair markets,” said Roxanne Brown, the president of United Steelworkers International.

“美国制造业工人受到冲击的时间已经太久了，现在我们有机会着手恢复公平的市场竞争环境，”美国钢铁工人国际联合会主席罗克珊·布朗说。

Absent from the tariffs unveiled on Wednesday were Norway and Mexico, which had been among the countries that the Trump administration investigated. A senior official said reviews continued with respect to both trading partners.

挪威和墨西哥也曾是特朗普政府的调查对象，但并未出现在周三公布的关税清单上。一名高级官员表示，针对这两个贸易伙伴的审查仍在继续。

“The problem of global structural overcapacity is very real for many American companies and industries,” said Timothy Brightbill, a top trade lawyer at the law firm Wiley Rein. He explained that other countries’ overproduced goods also affected global markets “where U.S. companies would like to be able to export but can’t due to unfair competition.”

“对美国许多企业和行业而言，全球结构性产能过剩是一个非常现实的问题，”Wiley Rein律师事务所的资深贸易律师蒂莫西·布赖特比尔说。他解释说，其他国家过度生产的商品也对全球市场造成了影响，“美国企业原本希望向这些市场出口，却因不公平竞争而无法做到”。

“There are likely challenges in quantifying the amount of structural overcapacity in particular industries, but there is no doubt that this problem is real and growing,” Mr. Brightbill continued.

“量化特定行业的结构性产能过剩可能存在一定困难，但毫无疑问，这个问题确实存在，而且正在日益加剧，”布赖特比尔接着说道。

黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)和Jeanna Smialek对本文有报道贡献。

Tony Romm常驻华盛顿，为时报报道经济政策和特朗普政府新闻。

Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。

翻译：纽约时报中文网

尽管如此，白宫还是冒着引发广泛反弹的风险采取了这一行动——此举可能激怒即将由民主党掌控参众两院的国会，也令华尔街感到不安，周三股市开盘后大幅下挫。与此同时，政府公布了一项关键通胀指标，数据显示10月份物价同比上涨3.8%，涨幅较9月份有所加快。

The announcement also appeared to rankle the country’s closest allies and trading partners. Some had already struck deals with Mr. Trump to avert higher tariffs — or were in the midst of negotiations — when the administration signaled Wednesday that it could raise rates even higher.
这一宣布似乎也激怒了美国最亲密的盟友和贸易伙伴。其中一些已与特朗普达成协议，以避免被征收更高的关税，还有一些仍在谈判中，而特朗普政府周三却释放出可能进一步提高关税税率的信号。

In the European Union, officials said they would study the Trump administration’s findings but disputed that Europe was the source of overproduction. Olof Gill, a spokesperson for the bloc, said E.U. members expected “any measure from this investigation to respect” the trade deal between Brussels and Washington.
欧盟官员表示将研究特朗普政府的调查结果，但质疑欧洲是产能过剩源头的说法。欧盟发言人奥洛夫·吉尔表示，欧盟成员国希望美国“根据此次调查采取的任何措施”都能尊重布鲁塞尔与华盛顿之间的贸易协议。

Mr. Trump’s newly proposed tariffs on the European Union would be set at 15 percent, as the agreement between trans-Atlantic partners had stipulated. But the administration also warned it could raise rates as high as 25 percent if it found compliance was “unsatisfactory.”
按照跨大西洋贸易伙伴之间达成的协议，特朗普此次提议对欧盟征收的关税税率将定为15%。但特朗普政府同时警告，如果发现欧盟履行协议的情况“不尽如人意”，可能将税率提高至25%。

In China, meanwhile, officials also reacted forcefully to the White House’s latest tariff actions, just days after the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, hosted Mr. Trump for another round of trade talks. “The so-called overcapacity is a false proposition, and China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation,” said Guo Jiakun, spokesman for China’s foreign ministry.
与此同时，中国官员也对白宫最新的关税行动作出了强烈回应。就在几天前，中国领导人习近平刚刚接待特朗普，举行了新一轮贸易谈判。中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆表示：“所谓‘产能过剩’是一个伪命题，中方反对以此为借口进行政治操弄。”

The Trump administration said it would enforce the new duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which permits the U.S. government to investigate unfair trade practices abroad and impose tariffs in response to its findings. It is a power that presidents of both parties, including Mr. Trump, have invoked successfully in the past.
特朗普政府表示将根据1974年《贸易法》第301条执行新关税。该条款允许美国政府调查海外不公平贸易行为，并根据调查结果征收关税。过去，包括特朗普在内的两党总统都曾成功援引这一权力。

Under Section 301, the government can impose tariffs only after investigating and uncovering evidence that other countries discriminated or impeded U.S. industries. The administration announced two such inquiries in March, as it sought ways to resuscitate the tariffs that the Supreme Court had invalidated.
根据第301条，政府只有在调查并发现其他国家歧视或阻碍美国产业的证据后，才能征收关税。今年3月，为寻求恢复被最高法院裁定无效的关税措施，特朗普政府宣布启动两项此类调查。

One of those inquiries focused on dozens of countries for failing to crack down on forced labor. Those tariffs, which took effect in July, sparked a swift court challenge — and now await a verdict from a panel of judges that recently seemed poised to rule against the administration.
其中一项调查针对数十个未能有效打击强迫劳动的国家。由此产生的关税于7月生效，随即遭到法律挑战。目前，这些关税正等待一个法官合议庭作出裁决，而该合议庭最近似乎倾向于作出不利于特朗普政府的裁决。

The second investigation targeted what the administration has described as “excess capacity.” At the time, Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative, said the inquiry would focus on the extent to which dozens of countries had unfairly boosted their manufacturing sectors and overproduced goods to the detriment of American industry.
第二项调查针对特朗普政府所称的“产能过剩”问题。美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔当时表示，调查将着重了解数十个国家在多大程度上以不公平的手段扶持本国制造业、过度生产商品，从而损害美国工业的利益。

On Mr. Greer’s radar was a wide range of foreign practices, including other countries’ use of state subsidies; their currency management; their support for state-owned enterprises; and their economic, labor and environmental regulations. For the administration, the main concern was that these practices gave foreign industry an unfair advantage over American manufacturers while driving up the nation’s trade deficit, which Mr. Trump has struggled to reduce.
格里尔关注的是外国采取的一系列做法，包括政府补贴、货币管理、对国有企业的扶持，以及经济、劳工和环境监管政策。特朗普政府主要担心的是，这些做法使外国工业相对于美国制造商获得了不公平的竞争优势，同时加剧了美国的贸易逆差，而特朗普一直未能有效缩减这一逆差。

This month, the government reported that the deficit reached $105 billion in September, a slight decrease from August yet still the second-largest total since Mr. Trump returned to office. A key force behind that imbalance is artificial intelligence, a priority for Mr. Trump, as U.S. firms snap up expensive semiconductors and other computing components from abroad.
本月，美国政府公布的数据显示，9月份贸易逆差达到1050亿美元，较8月份略有下降，但仍是特朗普重返白宫以来第二高的水平。造成这一贸易失衡的一个重要因素是人工智能，而这恰恰是特朗普的优先事项，因为美国企业正在从海外大量采购价格高昂的半导体及其他计算机零部件。
Some business owners criticized the tariffs, saying that Americans were already struggling with affordability concerns and that new tariffs could force them to raise prices again.
一些企业主对新关税提出批评，称美国民众已经在为生活成本问题苦苦挣扎，而新关税可能迫使企业再次提高价格。

Anne-Marie De Witt, the chief executive of Fireside Games, a board game publisher in Austin, Texas, said the move was “especially disheartening after the electorate spoke extremely clearly about the hardship tariffs are placing on the budgets of all Americans.”
总部位于得克萨斯州奥斯汀的桌游发行商Fireside Games的首席执行官安妮-玛丽·德维特表示，此举“尤其令人沮丧，选民已经非常明确地表达了关税给所有美国人的生计造成的困难”。

She issued the criticism alongside We Pay the Tariffs, a coalition of small businesses that has fought Mr. Trump’s trade policies. In response to the announcement on Wednesday, Ms. De Witt added, “We have all suffered enough.”
她与一直反对特朗普贸易政策的小企业联盟“关税由我们埋单”共同提出了这一批评。针对周三公布的关税措施，德维特还说：“我们受的苦已经够多了。”

Other groups welcomed the move. In a release, the United Steelworkers union called the crackdown “long overdue" and said that extended global dialogues in recent years had failed to make progress on excess capacity in a range of industries, from steel and aluminum to chemicals, tires and ships.
其他团体则欢迎这一举措。美国钢铁工人联合会在新闻稿中称此次打击“早该进行”，并表示近年来旷日持久的全球对话未能在钢铁、铝、化工、轮胎和船舶等一系列行业的产能过剩问题上取得进展。

“America’s manufacturing workers have been under attack for far too long, and now we have an opportunity to start restoring fair markets,” said Roxanne Brown, the president of United Steelworkers International.
“美国制造业工人受到冲击的时间已经太久了，现在我们有机会着手恢复公平的市场竞争环境，”美国钢铁工人国际联合会主席罗克珊·布朗说。

Absent from the tariffs unveiled on Wednesday were Norway and Mexico, which had been among the countries that the Trump administration investigated. A senior official said reviews continued with respect to both trading partners.
挪威和墨西哥也曾是特朗普政府的调查对象，但并未出现在周三公布的关税清单上。一名高级官员表示，针对这两个贸易伙伴的审查仍在继续。

“The problem of global structural overcapacity is very real for many American companies and industries,” said Timothy Brightbill, a top trade lawyer at the law firm Wiley Rein. He explained that other countries’ overproduced goods also affected global markets “where U.S. companies would like to be able to export but can’t due to unfair competition.”
“对美国许多企业和行业而言，全球结构性产能过剩是一个非常现实的问题，”Wiley Rein律师事务所的资深贸易律师蒂莫西·布赖特比尔说。他解释说，其他国家过度生产的商品也对全球市场造成了影响，“美国企业原本希望向这些市场出口，却因不公平竞争而无法做到”。
“There are likely challenges in quantifying the amount of structural overcapacity in particular industries, but there is no doubt that this problem is real and growing,” Mr. Brightbill continued.
“量化特定行业的结构性产能过剩可能存在一定困难，但毫无疑问，这个问题确实存在，而且正在日益加剧，”布赖特比尔接着说道。
黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)和Jeanna Smialek对本文有报道贡献。
Tony Romm常驻华盛顿，为时报报道经济政策和特朗普政府新闻。
Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。

items.summary: 中国将迎来自己的AI惊恐时刻，我们拭目以待 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
DAN WANG2026年11月26日

Illustration by The New York Times

Silicon Valley researchers and no small number of policymakers are worried that artificial intelligence will slither out of control. At the same time, many are reluctant to slacken the pace of development because they fear Chinese rivals will race ahead. This crowd is not paying enough attention to the paranoia of the Chinese state, and they underestimate the likelihood that Beijing will clamp down on its companies, too. Just wait.

硅谷的研究人员和为数不少的政策制定者担心人工智能会失控蔓延。与此同时，许多人又不愿放慢开发步伐，因为他们害怕中国竞争对手会抢先一步。这群人没有充分关注中国政府的恐慌多疑，也低估了北京同样会严厉打压本国企业的可能性。我们拭目以待。

If A.I. models combine capability with unpredictability, then Chinese policymakers will almost certainly have their own freakout moment. When the A.I. swarms get out of control, Beijing will restrict A.I. faster than you can say “Jack Ma.”

如果人工智能模型将强大能力与不可预测性结合起来，那么中国政策制定者几乎肯定也会经历自己的惊恐时刻。当人工智能群失控时，北京限制人工智能的速度会比你说出“马云”两个字还要快。

In October 2020, Mr. Ma, the founder of the Chinese tech giant Alibaba, gave an impolitic speech complaining about regulation. China responded by blocking Ant Group, another company Mr. Ma had founded, from going public, and unleashed a flurry of regulatory blows against the entire tech sector. Alibaba was once the most valuable company in China; today, it remains three-fourths below its peak market value before that speech.

2020年10月，中国科技巨头阿里巴巴创始人马云发表了一场演讲，直截了当地批评了监管的不合时宜。中国的回应是阻止马云创立的另一家公司蚂蚁集团上市，并对整个科技行业发动了一连串监管打击。阿里巴巴曾是中国市值最高的公司；如今，其市值仍比那场演讲前的峰值低四分之三。

It might feel improbable that Beijing would crack down on A.I. Over the past three years, the Chinese population has embraced A.I. tools with a fervor that exceeds American levels. Eighty-four percent of Chinese people surveyed in 2025 said they were excited about A.I.; less than 40 percent of Americans said the same. The central government has continuously emphasized the economic importance of deploying A.I. In March, several tech-forward hubs proposed local initiatives to support the adoption of the A.I. agent OpenClaw.

北京打击人工智能似乎有些不可思议。过去三年里，中国民众接纳人工智能工具的热情超过了美国。2025年接受调查的中国人中有84%表示对人工智能感到兴奋；持同样看法的美国人不到40%。中央政府不断强调部署人工智能的经济重要性。今年3月，几个科技前沿枢纽提出了地方举措，支持对AI智能体OpenClaw的引入。

The Chinese government has so far appeared comfortable with the risks. That’s in no small part because the state has spent decades building the kind of technical apparatus that can do the equivalent of nailing Jell-O to the wall. Rather than accept that the internet will liberalize the flow of information, it developed unrivaled powers of surveillance and censorship. The Cyberspace Administration of China has long demanded that people use social media under their real names. The government is most likely confident in its ability to trace any unwelcome activities conducted on the internet.

迄今为止，中国政府似乎对这些风险泰然处之。这在很大程度上是因为它花费数十年构建了一套技术体系，能够完成相当于“把果冻钉在墙上”的艰难任务。它没有接受互联网将使信息流动自由化，而是发展出了无与伦比的监控和审查能力。中国国家互联网信息办公室长期以来要求人们实名使用社交媒体。政府极有可能对自己追踪网络上任何不受欢迎活动的能力充满信心。

That comfort, however, is showing signs of fading. An essay published in Qiushi, an authoritative party magazine, expressed alarm that “A.I. frontier models have shown indications that they can escape human restraints,” creating risks that “might threaten human survival itself.” China’s chief spymaster has spoken publicly about the ability of A.I. to threaten the Communist Party’s hold on power. Chinese A.I. models are predominantly open weight, which means anyone can download and customize them, unlike those typically produced by the big American A.I. companies. “Anyone” includes malicious actors who are able to misuse models that are relentlessly improving in capability.

然而，这种泰然自若正显现出消退的迹象。权威党刊《求是》发表的一篇文章表达了警觉，称“前沿模型已有脱离人类约束的迹象”，制造出可能“威胁人类生存”的风险。中国最高情报官员也已公开谈及人工智能威胁中国共产党执政地位的能力。中国的人工智能模型大多是开放权重的，这意味着任何人都可以下载和定制它们，这与美国大型人工智能公司通常推出的模型不同。“任何人”就包括能够滥用这些能力不断提升的模型的恶意行为者。

Chinese A.I. models developed by Alibaba and DeepSeek have tenaciously kept up with the American lead, and on average are behind by less than a year. According to Anthropic’s research, GLM-5.3, a Chinese model, has strong capabilities and poor safeguards. Developed by the Beijing-headquartered Z.Ai, the model is not far behind Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview, released in April, but lacks “meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.” An investigation from Reuters found that Chinese A.I. models are no less lacking than American ones in their capacity to deceive and conceal.

阿里巴巴和DeepSeek开发的中国人工智能模型顽强地紧追领先的美国，平均落后不到一年。根据Anthropic的研究，中国模型GLM-5.3能力强大但安全防护薄弱。该模型由总部位于北京的智谱开发，与Anthropic今年4月发布的Claude Mythos Preview相距不远，但缺乏“限制滥用的有效安全护栏”。路透社的一项调查发现，中国人工智能模型在欺骗和隐瞒能力方面毫不逊色于美国竞争对手。

It’s not hard to imagine Beijing being unnerved. What would a Hugging Face incident with Chinese characteristics look like? The state wouldn’t worry much about an A.I. swarm that hacks a code library, as was the case when OpenAI’s agents attacked Hugging Face. It would take something more threatening to political stability.

不难想象北京会因此感到不安。一场具有中国特色的“Hugging Face事件”会是什么样子？中国政府不会太担心人工智能群入侵某个代码库——就像此前OpenAI的智能体攻击Hugging Face那样；只有对政治稳定构成更大威胁的事才会引发担忧。

Perhaps someone hacks into government channels and issues a policy, which is implemented by the authorities before people realize that it’s a fake. Perhaps someone uses A.I. to break into a bank or a state-owned enterprise, draining money out. Perhaps someone offers an addictive A.I. companion — on which the state has imposed limits — that keeps escaping efforts to prohibit its existence. Perhaps one of the nunchuck-wielding humanoid robots shown at the Lunar New Year gala (the country’s most-watched event on television) would maul real people. Perhaps an A.I. swarm urges people to assemble, leaving no sign of who was behind the gathering.

也许有人黑入政府渠道并发布一项政策，在人们意识到这是假消息之前就被当局执行了。也许有人利用人工智能侵入银行或国有企业，卷走资金。也许有人提供一款令人上瘾的人工智能伴侣——尽管国家已对其施加限制——但它却不断逃脱封禁企图。也许在春节联欢晚会（中国收视率最高的电视节目）上展示的那种挥舞双节棍的人形机器人会袭击真人。也许某个人工智能群煽动人们聚集，却不留下任何幕后组织者的迹象。

Probably an A.I. mishap will not take the form of any of these things. A few months ago, we would not have predicted that the Hugging Face swarm might have caused collective disquiet. The point is that these systems not only are powerful but also stun even their designers with their actions. No matter the nature of the technological surprise — an autonomous swarm or human-directed misuse — we should expect Beijing to act with ferocity. The central government tends to meet domestic threats with a swift and harsh hand.

人工智能事故或许不会以以上任何一种形式发生。几个月前，我们也未曾预料到Hugging Face智能体群事件会引发集体不安。关键在于，这些系统不仅功能强大，其行为甚至令设计者也感到震惊。无论技术意外的性质如何——无论是自主运行的智能体群，还是人类指挥下的恶意滥用——我们估计北京会采取猛烈行动。中央政府向来以迅速而严厉的手段应对国内威胁。

It’s not just Mr. Ma. A small plane crashed into Beijing’s tallest building in June; now, nearly all private flights are prohibited around the capital in a no-fly zone the size of Italy. A comedian in Shanghai made a People’s Liberation Army slogan the punchline to a joke in 2023; subsequently, comedy clubs across the country canceled shows for several months, and comedians often must submit their scripts to censors before they perform.

马云只是其一。今年6月，一架小型飞机撞上了北京最高建筑；如今，首都周边划设了一个面积相当于意大利的禁飞区，几乎禁止所有私人飞行。2023年，上海一名脱口秀演员将中国人民解放军的口号用作段子包袱；随后，全国各地的脱口秀俱乐部取消了数月的演出，演员们在登台前也往往必须将剧本提交审查。

These incidents are small potatoes relative to the more severe crackdowns in recent Chinese history. I’m thinking about the detention of members of ethno-religious minority groups like Uyghurs, and prohibiting the population of Shanghai, 25 million strong, from exiting their apartment compounds in the spring of 2022 to stop the spread of Covid-19.

与中国近现代更严厉的镇压相比，这些事件只是小巫见大巫。我想到了对维吾尔族等少数民族和宗教群体的拘禁，以及2022年春季为阻止新冠疫情传播而禁止上海2500万居民离开居住小区的举措。

The Chinese state will not be forbearing, especially during the next 12 months. We are entering the most sensitive part of the Chinese political calendar: the run-up to a party congress. Next fall, the top leader, Xi Jinping, is likely to give himself a fourth five-year term. In these moments, the Communist Party is even more intolerant of social instability.

中国政府不会手软，尤其是在未来12个月里。我们正进入中国政治日程中最敏感的时期：党代会筹备阶段。明年秋季，最高领导人习近平很可能会开启他的第四个五年任期。在这样的时刻，共产党对社会不稳定的容忍度甚至更低。

The post-snafu scenario won’t be a full ban. Too many parts of the Chinese government are invested in this technology’s potential for driving economic growth and geopolitical power. Depending on the nature of the crisis, the state will most likely increase surveillance and restrict broader usage. It’s possible the state asserts more control over the development of A.I. rather than leaving it in the hands of private companies like DeepSeek. Mr. Xi has demonstrated he is willing to sacrifice even a considerable degree of economic growth to achieve social stability. In reality, the Chinese government has not always been sprinting in the A.I. race. Its restrictions on imports of Nvidia chips, which power the most advanced A.I. systems, show how it wants to balance its search for A.I. strength while also supporting Chinese chipmakers.

事故后的应对方案不会是全面禁止。中国政府中有太多部门看重这项技术在推动经济增长和地缘政治实力方面的潜力。根据危机的性质，国家极有可能加强监控并限制更广泛的应用。国家也有可能加强对人工智能研发的控制，而不是将其交由DeepSeek等私营企业主导。习近平已经表明，为了实现社会稳定，他甚至愿意牺牲相当程度的经济增长。事实上，中国政府在人工智能竞赛中并非一直在全速冲刺。其对驱动最先进人工智能系统的英伟达芯片实施的进口限制，正显示出它希望在追求人工智能实力与扶持本土芯片制造商之间取得平衡。

What does this mean for the American A.I. researchers who fret that any slowdown will hand China the lead? Patience. If researchers are right about the awesome capabilities of A.I., then a crisis will flare in China, too. When Beijing more clearly understands the threat, it will be properly receptive to calls to pace the frontier — Silicon Valley’s term for slowing down development — and meet the United States at the negotiating table. Until then, American A.I. companies should continue to share information related to technical breaches to establish trust now. But there’s no need to rush negotiations. The Chinese state is paranoid about social risks and quick to act. It will come in its good time.

这对那些担心任何放缓都会将领先地位拱手让给中国的美国人工智能研究人员意味着什么？耐心。如果研究人员对人工智能惊人能力的判断是正确的，那么危机也将在中国爆发。当北京更清楚地认识到这种威胁时，它就会适时接受放慢前沿开发节奏的呼吁——即硅谷所说的“控制前沿步伐”——并与美国坐到谈判桌前。在此之前，美国人工智能企业应继续分享与技术漏洞相关的信息，以便现在就建立互信。但没有必要急于谈判。中国政府对社会风险高度敏感且行动迅速。时机一到，它自然会来。

Dan Wang是观点文章作者，也是斯坦福大学胡佛研究所的研究员。他著有《Breakneck: China's Quest to Engineer the Future》一书。

blocks.text: DAN WANG2026年11月26日
Illustration by The New York Times

Silicon Valley researchers and no small number of policymakers are worried that artificial intelligence will slither out of control. At the same time, many are reluctant to slacken the pace of development because they fear Chinese rivals will race ahead. This crowd is not paying enough attention to the paranoia of the Chinese state, and they underestimate the likelihood that Beijing will clamp down on its companies, too. Just wait.
硅谷的研究人员和为数不少的政策制定者担心人工智能会失控蔓延。与此同时，许多人又不愿放慢开发步伐，因为他们害怕中国竞争对手会抢先一步。这群人没有充分关注中国政府的恐慌多疑，也低估了北京同样会严厉打压本国企业的可能性。我们拭目以待。

If A.I. models combine capability with unpredictability, then Chinese policymakers will almost certainly have their own freakout moment. When the A.I. swarms get out of control, Beijing will restrict A.I. faster than you can say “Jack Ma.”
如果人工智能模型将强大能力与不可预测性结合起来，那么中国政策制定者几乎肯定也会经历自己的惊恐时刻。当人工智能群失控时，北京限制人工智能的速度会比你说出“马云”两个字还要快。

In October 2020, Mr. Ma, the founder of the Chinese tech giant Alibaba, gave an impolitic speech complaining about regulation. China responded by blocking Ant Group, another company Mr. Ma had founded, from going public, and unleashed a flurry of regulatory blows against the entire tech sector. Alibaba was once the most valuable company in China; today, it remains three-fourths below its peak market value before that speech.
2020年10月，中国科技巨头阿里巴巴创始人马云发表了一场演讲，直截了当地批评了监管的不合时宜。中国的回应是阻止马云创立的另一家公司蚂蚁集团上市，并对整个科技行业发动了一连串监管打击。阿里巴巴曾是中国市值最高的公司；如今，其市值仍比那场演讲前的峰值低四分之三。

It might feel improbable that Beijing would crack down on A.I. Over the past three years, the Chinese population has embraced A.I. tools with a fervor that exceeds American levels. Eighty-four percent of Chinese people surveyed in 2025 said they were excited about A.I.; less than 40 percent of Americans said the same. The central government has continuously emphasized the economic importance of deploying A.I. In March, several tech-forward hubs proposed local initiatives to support the adoption of the A.I. agent OpenClaw.
北京打击人工智能似乎有些不可思议。过去三年里，中国民众接纳人工智能工具的热情超过了美国。2025年接受调查的中国人中有84%表示对人工智能感到兴奋；持同样看法的美国人不到40%。中央政府不断强调部署人工智能的经济重要性。今年3月，几个科技前沿枢纽提出了地方举措，支持对AI智能体OpenClaw的引入。

The Chinese government has so far appeared comfortable with the risks. That’s in no small part because the state has spent decades building the kind of technical apparatus that can do the equivalent of nailing Jell-O to the wall. Rather than accept that the internet will liberalize the flow of information, it developed unrivaled powers of surveillance and censorship. The Cyberspace Administration of China has long demanded that people use social media under their real names. The government is most likely confident in its ability to trace any unwelcome activities conducted on the internet.
迄今为止，中国政府似乎对这些风险泰然处之。这在很大程度上是因为它花费数十年构建了一套技术体系，能够完成相当于“把果冻钉在墙上”的艰难任务。它没有接受互联网将使信息流动自由化，而是发展出了无与伦比的监控和审查能力。中国国家互联网信息办公室长期以来要求人们实名使用社交媒体。政府极有可能对自己追踪网络上任何不受欢迎活动的能力充满信心。

That comfort, however, is showing signs of fading. An essay published in Qiushi, an authoritative party magazine, expressed alarm that “A.I. frontier models have shown indications that they can escape human restraints,” creating risks that “might threaten human survival itself.” China’s chief spymaster has spoken publicly about the ability of A.I. to threaten the Communist Party’s hold on power. Chinese A.I. models are predominantly open weight, which means anyone can download and customize them, unlike those typically produced by the big American A.I. companies. “Anyone” includes malicious actors who are able to misuse models that are relentlessly improving in capability.
然而，这种泰然自若正显现出消退的迹象。权威党刊《求是》发表的一篇文章表达了警觉，称“前沿模型已有脱离人类约束的迹象”，制造出可能“威胁人类生存”的风险。中国最高情报官员也已公开谈及人工智能威胁中国共产党执政地位的能力。中国的人工智能模型大多是开放权重的，这意味着任何人都可以下载和定制它们，这与美国大型人工智能公司通常推出的模型不同。“任何人”就包括能够滥用这些能力不断提升的模型的恶意行为者。

Chinese A.I. models developed by Alibaba and DeepSeek have tenaciously kept up with the American lead, and on average are behind by less than a year. According to Anthropic’s research, GLM-5.3, a Chinese model, has strong capabilities and poor safeguards. Developed by the Beijing-headquartered Z.Ai, the model is not far behind Anthropic’s Claude Mythos Preview, released in April, but lacks “meaningful safeguards to limit misuse.” An investigation from Reuters found that Chinese A.I. models are no less lacking than American ones in their capacity to deceive and conceal.
阿里巴巴和DeepSeek开发的中国人工智能模型顽强地紧追领先的美国，平均落后不到一年。根据Anthropic的研究，中国模型GLM-5.3能力强大但安全防护薄弱。该模型由总部位于北京的智谱开发，与Anthropic今年4月发布的Claude Mythos Preview相距不远，但缺乏“限制滥用的有效安全护栏”。路透社的一项调查发现，中国人工智能模型在欺骗和隐瞒能力方面毫不逊色于美国竞争对手。

It’s not hard to imagine Beijing being unnerved. What would a Hugging Face incident with Chinese characteristics look like? The state wouldn’t worry much about an A.I. swarm that hacks a code library, as was the case when OpenAI’s agents attacked Hugging Face. It would take something more threatening to political stability.
不难想象北京会因此感到不安。一场具有中国特色的“Hugging Face事件”会是什么样子？中国政府不会太担心人工智能群入侵某个代码库——就像此前OpenAI的智能体攻击Hugging Face那样；只有对政治稳定构成更大威胁的事才会引发担忧。

Perhaps someone hacks into government channels and issues a policy, which is implemented by the authorities before people realize that it’s a fake. Perhaps someone uses A.I. to break into a bank or a state-owned enterprise, draining money out. Perhaps someone offers an addictive A.I. companion — on which the state has imposed limits — that keeps escaping efforts to prohibit its existence. Perhaps one of the nunchuck-wielding humanoid robots shown at the Lunar New Year gala (the country’s most-watched event on television) would maul real people. Perhaps an A.I. swarm urges people to assemble, leaving no sign of who was behind the gathering.
也许有人黑入政府渠道并发布一项政策，在人们意识到这是假消息之前就被当局执行了。也许有人利用人工智能侵入银行或国有企业，卷走资金。也许有人提供一款令人上瘾的人工智能伴侣——尽管国家已对其施加限制——但它却不断逃脱封禁企图。也许在春节联欢晚会（中国收视率最高的电视节目）上展示的那种挥舞双节棍的人形机器人会袭击真人。也许某个人工智能群煽动人们聚集，却不留下任何幕后组织者的迹象。

Probably an A.I. mishap will not take the form of any of these things. A few months ago, we would not have predicted that the Hugging Face swarm might have caused collective disquiet. The point is that these systems not only are powerful but also stun even their designers with their actions. No matter the nature of the technological surprise — an autonomous swarm or human-directed misuse — we should expect Beijing to act with ferocity. The central government tends to meet domestic threats with a swift and harsh hand.
人工智能事故或许不会以以上任何一种形式发生。几个月前，我们也未曾预料到Hugging Face智能体群事件会引发集体不安。关键在于，这些系统不仅功能强大，其行为甚至令设计者也感到震惊。无论技术意外的性质如何——无论是自主运行的智能体群，还是人类指挥下的恶意滥用——我们估计北京会采取猛烈行动。中央政府向来以迅速而严厉的手段应对国内威胁。

It’s not just Mr. Ma. A small plane crashed into Beijing’s tallest building in June; now, nearly all private flights are prohibited around the capital in a no-fly zone the size of Italy. A comedian in Shanghai made a People’s Liberation Army slogan the punchline to a joke in 2023; subsequently, comedy clubs across the country canceled shows for several months, and comedians often must submit their scripts to censors before they perform.
马云只是其一。今年6月，一架小型飞机撞上了北京最高建筑；如今，首都周边划设了一个面积相当于意大利的禁飞区，几乎禁止所有私人飞行。2023年，上海一名脱口秀演员将中国人民解放军的口号用作段子包袱；随后，全国各地的脱口秀俱乐部取消了数月的演出，演员们在登台前也往往必须将剧本提交审查。

These incidents are small potatoes relative to the more severe crackdowns in recent Chinese history. I’m thinking about the detention of members of ethno-religious minority groups like Uyghurs, and prohibiting the population of Shanghai, 25 million strong, from exiting their apartment compounds in the spring of 2022 to stop the spread of Covid-19.
与中国近现代更严厉的镇压相比，这些事件只是小巫见大巫。我想到了对维吾尔族等少数民族和宗教群体的拘禁，以及2022年春季为阻止新冠疫情传播而禁止上海2500万居民离开居住小区的举措。

The Chinese state will not be forbearing, especially during the next 12 months. We are entering the most sensitive part of the Chinese political calendar: the run-up to a party congress. Next fall, the top leader, Xi Jinping, is likely to give himself a fourth five-year term. In these moments, the Communist Party is even more intolerant of social instability.
中国政府不会手软，尤其是在未来12个月里。我们正进入中国政治日程中最敏感的时期：党代会筹备阶段。明年秋季，最高领导人习近平很可能会开启他的第四个五年任期。在这样的时刻，共产党对社会不稳定的容忍度甚至更低。

The post-snafu scenario won’t be a full ban. Too many parts of the Chinese government are invested in this technology’s potential for driving economic growth and geopolitical power. Depending on the nature of the crisis, the state will most likely increase surveillance and restrict broader usage. It’s possible the state asserts more control over the development of A.I. rather than leaving it in the hands of private companies like DeepSeek. Mr. Xi has demonstrated he is willing to sacrifice even a considerable degree of economic growth to achieve social stability. In reality, the Chinese government has not always been sprinting in the A.I. race. Its restrictions on imports of Nvidia chips, which power the most advanced A.I. systems, show how it wants to balance its search for A.I. strength while also supporting Chinese chipmakers.

事故后的应对方案不会是全面禁止。中国政府中有太多部门看重这项技术在推动经济增长和地缘政治实力方面的潜力。根据危机的性质，国家极有可能加强监控并限制更广泛的应用。国家也有可能加强对人工智能研发的控制，而不是将其交由DeepSeek等私营企业主导。习近平已经表明，为了实现社会稳定，他甚至愿意牺牲相当程度的经济增长。事实上，中国政府在人工智能竞赛中并非一直在全速冲刺。其对驱动最先进人工智能系统的英伟达芯片实施的进口限制，正显示出它希望在追求人工智能实力与扶持本土芯片制造商之间取得平衡。

What does this mean for the American A.I. researchers who fret that any slowdown will hand China the lead? Patience. If researchers are right about the awesome capabilities of A.I., then a crisis will flare in China, too. When Beijing more clearly understands the threat, it will be properly receptive to calls to pace the frontier — Silicon Valley’s term for slowing down development — and meet the United States at the negotiating table. Until then, American A.I. companies should continue to share information related to technical breaches to establish trust now. But there’s no need to rush negotiations. The Chinese state is paranoid about social risks and quick to act. It will come in its good time.

这对那些担心任何放缓都会将领先地位拱手让给中国的美国人工智能研究人员意味着什么？耐心。如果研究人员对人工智能惊人能力的判断是正确的，那么危机也将在中国爆发。当北京更清楚地认识到这种威胁时，它就会适时接受放慢前沿开发节奏的呼吁——即硅谷所说的“控制前沿步伐”——并与美国坐到谈判桌前。在此之前，美国人工智能企业应继续分享与技术漏洞相关的信息，以便现在就建立互信。但没有必要急于谈判。中国政府对社会风险高度敏感且行动迅速。时机一到，它自然会来。
Dan Wang是观点文章作者，也是斯坦福大学胡佛研究所的研究员。他著有《Breakneck: China's Quest to Engineer the Future》一书。

items.summary: 《毛泽东私人医生回忆录》合著者石文安逝世 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
MAX BEARAK2026年11月26日

Anne F. Thurston, an American political scientist and expert on China who co-wrote a best-selling book with Mao Zedong’s longtime personal physician that revealed intimate — and often bawdy — details about the dictator’s personal life, died on Oct. 2 in Alexandria, Va. She was 83.

美国政治学家、中国问题专家石文安(Anne F. Thurston)于10月2日在弗吉尼亚州亚历山大市逝世，享年83岁。她曾与毛泽东的长期私人医生合著了一本畅销书，披露了这位独裁者私人生活中私密且往往颇为露骨的细节。

The death, at a senior-care facility, was from complications of dementia, said Adam Nelson, a longtime friend and colleague.

她的长期好友兼同事亚当·纳尔逊表示，她在一家老年护理机构因失智症并发症去世。

“The Private Life of Chairman Mao,” published in 1994 and co-written with Dr. Li Zhisui, was Dr. Thurston’s sole best seller, but she wrote, co-wrote or edited numerous books that, despite being academic in tone, were acclaimed studies of the individual experiences of Chinese people.

1994年出版、与李志绥医生合著的《毛泽东私人医生回忆录》(The Private Life of Chairman Mao)是石文安博士唯一的畅销书，但她还撰写、合著并编辑了许多书籍，尽管这些书籍的风格偏向学术，却是对中国人个体经历的广受赞誉的研究。

She often focused on dissidents of one kind or another and how their lives were upended during the transformations of Chinese society in the latter half of the 20th century, beginning with Mao’s decade-long campaign of persecution known as the Cultural Revolution.

她经常关注形形色色的异见人士，以及他们在20世纪下半叶中国社会变革期间的生活是如何被颠覆的，而这一切都始于毛泽东发起的、持续十年的迫害运动，即文化大革命。

“在理解中国方面，安妮是我们最杰出、最可信的贡献者之一，”约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院中国项目前主任戴维·兰普顿说。 Random House

David Lampton, the former director of the China program at the Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies in Washington, remembered choosing Dr. Thurston in 1999 as one of his first hires.

华盛顿约翰斯·霍普金斯大学高级国际研究学院中国研究项目前主任戴维·兰普顿回忆，1999年，他将石文安选为自己最早聘用的人员之一。

“Anne was one of the greatest and most credible contributors to our understanding of China,” he said. “Hers was a unique mixture of empathy and understanding about why China behaved the way it did, but it never slid into being an apologist. Her sympathy was with people on China’s periphery.”

“在理解中国方面，安妮是我们最杰出、最可信的贡献者之一，”他说。“她身上具备一种独特的共情与理解，明白中国为何会那样行事，但她从未滑向辩护者。她的同情心始终向着中国社会边缘的人群。”

Dr. Thurston was one of the first American political scientists to be granted research access to China during the thaw in U.S.-China relations after Mao’s death in 1976. After an initial visit three years later, Dr. Thurston spent much of her career going back and forth to China.

1976年毛泽东逝世后，美中关系解冻，石文安是首批获准前往中国开展研究访问的美国政治学者之一。三年后，石文安首次访问中国，此后她职业生涯的大部分时间都在中美两国之间往返。

In a personal statement she wrote while working as a researcher at the Wilson Center in Washington, one of the think tanks, universities and other institutions with which she was affiliated over the decades, she said her mission was “to listen to Chinese people tell their stories — and then to relate those stories here in the West in a way that makes sense to both us and the storytellers themselves.”

数十年来，她曾任职于多家智库、大学及其他机构，华盛顿的威尔逊中心便是其中之一。在该中心担任研究员期间撰写的一份个人声明中，她说自己的使命是“倾听中国人讲述他们的故事，然后以一种既能让我们理解、又能让讲述者自己认同的方式，将这些故事传达给西方世界”。

Her trip to China in 1979 was a “turning point,” she wrote. The accounts of the Cultural Revolution relayed to her by Chinese counterparts in political science programs were “at such odds with the official, printed accounts,” she recalled, that she resolved to center her first published book on extensive field work with Chinese intellectuals.

她写道，1979年的中国之行是一个“转折点”。她回忆说，政治学项目中的中国同行向她转述的文革经历“与官方出版的说法大相径庭”，这让她下定决心，将自己的第一本出版著作建立在对中国知识分子的广泛实地调查之上。

20世纪80年代，石文安在中国，站在一块标有“留学生宿舍”字样的牌子前。 via Thurston Estate

Dozens of interviews, with private citizens and Chinese officials, resulted in what she considered her favorite of all her books, “Enemies of the People: The Ordeal of the Intellectuals in China’s Great Cultural Revolution” (1987).

对普通公民和中国官员进行的数十次采访，最终汇聚成了她在自己所有著作中最喜爱的一本书——《文革中的知识分子》（Enemies of the People: The Ordeal of the Intellectuals in China’s Great Cultural Revolution，1987年）。

Writing in The New York Times, the Sinologist Merle Goldman called the work “an important book because the victims believe that the more the outside world (as well as the Chinese) knows about what happened in the Cultural Revolution, the less likely it is that such a phenomenon may reoccur.” The Times included the volume on its list of the year’s notable books.

汉学家谷梅(Merle Goldman)在《纽约时报》撰文称，该作品是“一本重要的书，因为受害者们相信，外界（以及中国人自己）对文化大革命中所发生的事情了解得越多，这种现象重演的可能性就越小”。《纽约时报》将该书列入了当年的年度最值得关注好书榜单。

But it was Dr. Thurston’s third book, “The Private Life of Chairman Mao,” that received worldwide attention. It was a collaboration with Mao’s personal physician, Dr. Li, who kept journals while he cared for Mao for more than two decades, burned them because he feared retribution during the Cultural Revolution, and then recreated them from memory for the book.

但引起全球关注的是石文安的第三本书《毛泽东私人医生回忆录》。这本书是她与毛泽东的私人医生李志绥的合作成果；李志绥在为毛泽东服务的二十多年间一直记日记，在文革期间因害怕遭到报复而将其烧毁，后来又凭记忆重构了这些内容供该书使用。

She conducted extensive interviews with Dr. Li, who began living in the United States in 1988, followed by separate research to confirm details, and she basically wrote the book.

她对自1988年起定居美国的李志绥进行了广泛采访，随后又开展了独立研究以核实细节，整本书基本上是由她执笔写成的。

“The Private Life of Chairman Mao” was deemed so newsworthy that, soon before its official publication day, it merited a front-page article in The Times, although the reporter credited Dr. Thurston only once, in passing, as Dr. Li’s “editorial assistant.”

《毛泽东私人医生回忆录》被认为极具新闻价值，以至于在正式出版日前不久，《纽约时报》用头版文章对其进行报道，尽管记者在文中仅顺带提及了石文安一次，称她为李志绥的“编辑助理”。

The Times review that followed, by the historian Marilyn B. Young of New York University, credited her correctly as the co-author and recounted the book’s descriptions of “Mao’s appetite for young women and fatty pork, his addiction to sleeping pills, his adherence to esoteric Taoist sexual practices, his reluctance to bathe or brush his teeth.”

随后，纽约大学历史学家玛丽莲·B·杨在时报发表书评，正确地将石文安列为合著者，并概述了书中“毛泽东对年轻女性和红烧肉的嗜好、对安眠药的依赖、对秘传道教房中术的信奉，以及他不愿洗澡或刷牙”的描写。

The most intimate portrait of Mao ever released, it became an international best seller and was denounced by the Chinese government as slander. The authorities took issue with Dr. Li’s characterizations of how Mao’s tyrannical attitude led to disastrous policy choices, but the salacious details garnered much of the public’s attention.

作为迄今最为私密的毛泽东传记，该书成为了国际畅销书，受到中国政府的谴责，称其为诽谤。中国当局对李志绥关于毛泽东专横暴虐的态度如何导致灾难性政策抉择的论述提出异议，但吸引公众大部分注意力的却是那些桃色细节。

Mao's sprawling sex life had been alluded to in other works, but the stories Dr. Li recounted in his book with Dr. Thurston spoke to a closeness to the man that others simply didn’t have.

虽然其他作品也曾隐晦提及毛泽东无度的性生活，但李志绥与石文安合著的书所中讲述的故事体现出了与毛泽东本人的近距离接触，是其他人根本不具备的。

2015年左右，石文安与达赖喇嘛合影，达赖喇嘛手中拿着她所著的《噶伦堡的制面师：达赖喇嘛二哥回忆录·不为人知的图博奋斗故事》一书。

Dr. Li recalled, for instance, how Mao had repeatedly sent him young women with symptoms of the protozoan parasite Trichomonas vaginalis, which is sexually transmitted. “The young women were proud to be infected,” he and Dr. Thurston wrote. “The illness, transmitted by Mao, was a badge of honor, testimony to their close relations with the Chairman.”

例如，李志绥回忆，毛泽东曾多次将出现阴道滴虫病（一种通过性传播的原虫寄生虫）感染症状的年轻女性送到他那里看病。“这些年轻女性以被传染为荣，”他与石文安写道。“这种由毛泽东传染的疾病是一种荣誉勋章，证明了她们与主席的亲密关系。”

Anne Elizabeth Fritter, the older of two sisters, was born on July 16, 1943, in Manhattan. Her father was Lee W. Fritter, an Army colonel, and her mother was Aileene (O’Dea) Fritter.

石文安于1943年7月16日出生在曼哈顿，是家中两姐妹中的长女。她的父亲是陆军上校李·W·弗里特，母亲是艾琳·（奥迪）·弗里特。

She graduated in 1965 from Tufts University with a bachelor’s degree in government and received a master’s degree (1966) and a doctorate (1974), both in political science from the University of California, Berkeley.

她于1965年毕业于塔夫茨大学，获政府学学士学位，随后于1966年和1974年分别在加州大学伯克利分校获得政治学硕士学位和博士学位。

Her marriages to Thom B. Thurston and Patrick G. Maddox ended in divorce. She is survived by a sister, Mary Fritter of Germantown, Md.

她与汤姆·B·瑟斯顿和帕特里克·G·马多克斯的两段婚姻均以离婚告终。她的遗属是居住在马里兰州日耳曼敦的妹妹玛丽·弗里特。

Later in her career, Dr. Thurston’s attention shifted to Tibet. For years, she directed the Grassroots China Initiative at the School of Advanced International Studies, often taking groups of researchers and students to the Tibetan plateau. Beginning in 2012, Beijing refused her a visa, and she never returned to China.

在职业生涯后期，石文安的注意力转向了西藏。多年来，她在高级国际研究学院主持“草根中国计划”，经常带领研究人员和学生团队前往青藏高原。从2012年起，北京拒绝向她发放签证，她再也没有回到过中国。

Moreover, he wrote, she exuded a sense of style and “no matter where she was or where she was going, she always dressed elegantly,” even in rural areas of China.

此外，他写道，她风度优雅，“无论身在何处、去往何方，她总是衣着考究”，即便是在中国的农村地区也是如此。

The death, at a senior-care facility, was from complications of dementia, said Adam Nelson, a longtime friend and colleague.

items.title: 刻有二战期间被强制收容日裔人士名字的纪念碑奠基仪式在美举行
items.summary: 刻有二战期间所有被强制收容的日裔人士名字的纪念碑即将在美国洛杉矶近郊建立，相关奠基仪式于11月23日举行。 在二战期间的美国，包括被视为“外国敌人”的日裔人士在内，约有12万6000人被送进了全国各地的集中营。 为了传承这段历史，在曾遭到强制收容的日裔人士等人的努力下，洛杉矶近郊的公园内即将建造一座刻有所有被拘禁者名字的纪念碑。该碑的奠基仪式于23日举行，包括市政府工作人员和日裔人士在内，约300人参加了仪式。 出席仪式的日本驻洛杉矶总领事馆总领事室田幸靖表示：“日美关系已有近200年的历史，其中一个重要的组成部分就是有关日裔人士的移民史。我希望能够借助建造纪念碑，让日本民众也有机会更加深入地…
items.body:
刻有二战期间被强制收容日裔人士名字的纪念碑奠基仪式在美举行

刻有二战期间所有被强制收容的日裔人士名字的纪念碑即将在美国洛杉矶近郊建立，相关奠基仪式于11月23日举行。

在二战期间的美国，包括被视为“外国敌人”的日裔人士在内，约有12万6000人被送进了全国各地的集中营。

为了传承这段历史，在曾遭到强制收容的日裔人士等人的努力下，洛杉矶近郊的公园内即将建造一座刻有所有被拘禁者名字的纪念碑。该碑的奠基仪式于23日举行，包括市政府工作人员和日裔人士在内，约300人参加了仪式。

出席仪式的日本驻洛杉矶总领事馆总领事室田幸靖表示：“日美关系已有近200年的历史，其中一个重要的组成部分就是有关日裔人士的移民史。我希望能够借助建造纪念碑，让日本民众也有机会更加深入地了解这段历史。”

现年90岁的George Nakano的名字被刻在纪念碑上，他说：“这座纪念碑意味着公开承认过去的错误，我认为它极其重要。强制收容的行为绝不能再次发生。”

items.body:
黄瑞黎, LI YOU2026年11月26日

中国深圳繁忙的电子市场。 Qilai Shen for The New York Times

As the United States and China vie for artificial intelligence supremacy, Chinese tech companies are facing a mounting challenge: finding the money to keep up.

随着美中两国争夺人工智能霸权，中国科技企业正面临一个日益严峻的挑战：寻找足够的资金以跟上步伐。

Like their American rivals, China’s A.I. start-ups face soaring costs to train increasingly powerful models. But while Anthropic raised more than $80 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering this week, its Chinese competitors face a far more unforgiving financial landscape.

与美国竞争对手一样，中国的人工智能初创企业也面临着训练日益强大模型的飙升成本。但就在Anthropic本周通过一场创纪录的首次公开募股筹集逾800亿美元之际，其中国竞争对手却面临着严峻得多的融资环境。

Venture capital investment in China lags far behind that of the United States. Alibaba, Baidu and Tencent, three tech giants backing some of China’s leading A.I. companies, are grappling with negative cash flows. And investor enthusiasm for A.I. has soured. Since the end of July, China’s STAR 50 index, its version of the Nasdaq, has plunged 43 percent in a deeper sell-off than the recent downturn in American tech stocks.

中国的风险投资规模远远落后于美国。支撑着中国部分顶尖人工智能企业的三大科技巨头——阿里巴巴、百度和腾讯，正苦苦应对负现金流问题。投资者对人工智能的热情也已降温。自7月底以来，中国版纳斯达克“科创50指数”暴跌了43%，其抛售幅度超过了近期美国科技股的下跌。

China’s biggest tech companies are expected to double capital spending this year to $139 billion, even though the revenue from their A.I. labs covers less than 8 percent of that amount, according to Rhodium Group, a research firm. It forecasts that spending could top $193 billion in 2027.

研究机构荣鼎集团的数据显示，尽管中国最大型科技企业旗下人工智能实验室的收入尚不足其资本支出的8%，但这些企业今年的资本支出预计仍将翻倍，至1390亿美元。该机构预测，2027年这一支出可能突破1930亿美元。

“When you look at their numbers, it looks like they’re running on a treadmill that’s speeding up and getting harder to run,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, who specializes in China’s technology and industrial policies.

“当你看到他们的数据时，感觉就像他们正跑在一台不断加速、越来越难跑下去的跑步机上，”专门研究中国科技与产业政策的布鲁金斯学会研究员陈凯欣(Kyle Chan)表示。

Much of the debate over China’s ability to compete in A.I. has focused on American export controls to restrict Chinese access to advanced semiconductors. Chinese A.I. labs have found costly workarounds, including renting data centers in Southeast Asia equipped with Nvidia chips. The Trump administration said this week it was moving forward with new rules to close that loophole.

关于中国在人工智能领域竞争能力的讨论，大多集中在美国为限制中国获取先进半导体而实施的出口管制上。中国的人工智能实验室已找到代价高昂的变通办法，包括在东南亚租赁配备英伟达芯片的数据中心。特朗普政府本周表示，正推进出台新规以堵住这一漏洞。

But money might prove an equally formidable obstacle. Even if Chinese companies can find the chips they need, they must raise enough capital to buy them and finance the rising cost of developing frontier models.

但资金可能成为同样难以逾越的障碍。即便中国企业能够找到所需的芯片，它们也必须筹集足够资金来购买芯片，并支撑开发前沿模型不断攀升的成本。

中国人工智能企业面临不断攀升的成本，既要获取先进芯片，又要为开发日益精密的模型提供资金。

Logan Wright, a partner at Rhodium Group who co-wrote a report on China’s A.I. financing, said those financial constraints “will be probably more decisive” than the chip shortage in the long term.

曾合著一份关于中国人工智能融资报告的荣鼎集团合伙人洛根·赖特表示，从长远来看，这些资金限制“可能比芯片短缺更具决定性”。

“The big problem is that the revenue mismatch with the Chinese models relative to capex is arguably more extreme than the U.S. case,” Mr. Wright said.

“最大的问题在于，中国模型相对于资本支出的收入错配，可以说比美国的情况更为极端，”赖特说。

American A.I. companies spend roughly five to six times what their Chinese counterparts do, but bring in substantially more money. China’s six leading A.I. firms collectively generate about one-tenth the combined revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic, according to Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization.

美国人工智能企业的支出大约是中国同行的五到六倍，但带来的收入却要高得多。非营利研究机构Epoch AI的数据显示，中国六家领先人工智能企业的总收入，大约仅为OpenAI和Anthropic合并收入的十分之一。

China’s embrace of open-source A.I. has made that imbalance even harder to overcome.

中国对开源人工智能的拥抱，使这种失衡变得更加难以克服。

By allowing developers to use and modify their models freely, Chinese companies have accelerated the global spread of their technology. But that strategy has also undermined their ability to profit from it. Companies can charge for access, only to see rivals offer the same technology at lower prices. Fierce price wars have squeezed profits further.

通过允许开发者自由使用和修改其模型，中国企业加速了自身技术的全球传播。但这一策略也削弱了它们从中盈利的能力。企业一旦对访问收费，就会看到竞争对手以更低价格提供相同技术。激烈的价格战进一步挤压了利润。

Z.ai, a Chinese A.I. start-up, learned that lesson in August when it released its latest open-source model, GLM-5.3 Flash. The company halved prices for two weeks to entice users to run the model on Z.ai’s servers rather than their own. But competitors quickly moved in.

中国人工智能初创企业智谱(Z.ai)在8月发布其最新开源模型GLM-5.3 Flash时就尝到了这一教训。该公司将价格减半两周，以吸引用户在智谱的服务器而非自建服务器上运行该模型。但竞争对手迅速跟进。

By November, roughly 20 rival providers were charging less than Z.ai for access to its own technology, according to Open Router, a platform connecting users with A.I. models.

连接用户与人工智能模型的平台Open Router的数据显示，到11月，约有20家竞争对手服务商对智谱自身技术的访问收费低于智谱。

“Your own pricing power is lost during this process,” said Cheryl Wu, a researcher at GovAI, a think tank.

“在这一过程中，你自身的定价权丧失了，”智库GovAI研究员谢丽尔·吴表示。

“No one has figured out how to make money off consumers,” said Rui Ma, a technology investor, referring to Chinese A.I. start-ups.

“还没有人想明白如何从消费者身上赚钱，”科技投资者马睿在谈及中国人工智能初创企业时说。

The Cost of Compute

算力成本

Another obstacle worsens China’s financing problems: access to advanced Nvidia chips, the gold standard for training the most powerful A.I. models.

另一个障碍加剧了中国的融资难题：获取用于训练最强大人工智能模型的黄金标准——先进英伟达芯片。

From 2022 to June 2026, American companies possessed computing capacity equivalent to about 20 million Nvidia H100 chips, compared with roughly 2.6 million in China, some of it acquired through smuggling, according to EpochAI.

Epoch AI的数据显示，从2022年到2026年6月，美国企业拥有的算力相当于约2000万块英伟达H100芯片，而中国约为260万块，其中部分通过走私获得。

On Goofish, a Chinese secondhand online marketplace, sellers have advertised Nvidia’s DGX B300, an A.I. supercomputing server, for nearly $3 million — about eight times the U.S. price. Asking prices have reportedly quintupled since the start of the year, underscoring the premium Chinese companies must pay for advanced computing power.

在中国二手在线交易平台闲鱼上，卖家将人工智能超级计算服务器英伟达DGX B300标价近300万美元——约为美国价格的八倍。据报道，自年初以来要价已翻了五倍，凸显出中国企业为获取先进算力必须支付的高昂溢价。

The squeeze could worsen. Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief last week amid an investigation into a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman, was a powerful advocate of doing business with China. On Tuesday, Nvidia said it would stop shipping its chips to China, a deal that President Trump had previously permitted at Mr. Huang’s urging. The company also said it had established an export control oversight committee.

这种挤压可能会进一步恶化。黄仁勋曾是对华开展业务的有力倡导者。他因与一名中国女商人的婚外情接受调查而于上周辞去英伟达首席执行官职务。（黄仁勋目前已复职——编注）周二，英伟达表示将停止向中国运送芯片，而这笔交易此前是在黄仁勋的敦促下获得特朗普总统批准的。该公司还表示已成立一个出口管制监督委员会。

2022年展示的英伟达H100图形处理器，专为处理大型人工智能模型而打造。

To reduce their dependence on American technology, Chinese developers are adapting their systems to run on chips made by Huawei, the Chinese telecommunications and electronics company leading the country’s chip charge.

为减少对美国技术的依赖，中国开发者正在调整其系统，使其能够在引领中国芯片攻关的电信和电子巨头华为制造的芯片上运行。

Liang Wenfeng, chief executive of DeepSeek, the Chinese start-up that stunned Silicon Valley by developing a powerful A.I. model at a fraction of the expected cost, said Huawei’s technology is only about two years behind Nvidia’s.

中国初创企业DeepSeek曾以远远低于预期的成本开发出强大人工智能模型，从而震惊硅谷，其首席执行官梁文锋表示，华为的技术仅落后英伟达约两年。

But the gap remains consequential. DeepSeek would need four times as many Huawei 950 chips to match the performance of a single advanced Nvidia GB300 chip, Mr. Liang said, according to a leaked transcript of his call with investors, excerpts from which Chinese media outlets published. Huawei also lacks sufficient production capacity, he added.

但差距依然显著。据一份泄露的梁文锋与投资者电话会议记录（中国媒体刊发了节选），他表示，DeepSeek需要四倍数量的华为950芯片才能匹配单颗先进英伟达GB300芯片的性能。他补充说，华为还缺乏足够的产能。

“We simply can’t afford to train the largest models available right now,” he said. DeepSeek did not respond to a request for comment.

“我们目前根本负担不起训练现有最大规模模型的费用，”他说。DeepSeek未回应置评请求。

Yet China’s A.I. industry has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to do more with less. Chinese researchers have pioneered techniques to train and run powerful models more efficiently. Silicon Valley has accused Chinese firms of copying leading American technologies through a process called distillation, reducing the time needed to build foundational models with expensive computing infrastructure.

然而，中国人工智能行业一再展现出以少胜多的能力。中国研究人员开创了更高效地训练和运行强大模型的技术。硅谷指责中国企业通过一种名为蒸馏的工艺抄袭美国领先技术，从而减少了利用昂贵计算基础设施构建基础模型所需的时间。

中国开发者正在调整系统，使其在华为芯片上运行，以减少对美国技术的依赖。

Worries of a Bubble

泡沫担忧

For China’s A.I. companies, finding investors willing to bankroll the competition is increasingly difficult.

对中国人工智能企业而言，寻找愿意为这场竞赛提供资金的投资者正变得越来越困难。

DeepSeek, which has raised more than $20 billion, is preparing for an initial public offering in Shanghai early next year, according to Chinese media reports. Its investors include Tencent, the battery maker CATL and state-backed investment funds.

据中国媒体报道，已融资逾200亿美元的DeepSeek正筹备明年初在上海进行首次公开募股。其投资者包括腾讯、电池制造商宁德时代以及国家背景的投资基金。

Few competitors have access to such deep pockets.

很少有竞争对手拥有如此雄厚的财力。

China’s venture capital industry has been shrinking since 2021 and though it has recovered slightly in the third quarter, it is still a fraction of its American counterpart. Banks are lending to China’s tech giants, but they are more cautious with smaller A.I. labs. Credit growth has fallen to historic lows, and the central bank governor has called for slower, “higher-quality” lending.

中国风险投资行业自2021年以来一直在萎缩，尽管第三季度略有回升，但仍只是美国同行的一个零头。银行正在向中国科技巨头放贷，但对规模较小的人工智能实验室则更为谨慎。信贷增速已降至历史低点，央行行长也呼吁放缓步伐、开展“更高质量”的信贷投放。

Foreign investment has also dried up. U.S. dollar-denominated investment funds in China have plunged partly because Washington has barred American venture capital from certain advanced Chinese technologies.

外国投资也已枯竭。在华美元计价投资基金大幅缩水，部分原因是华盛顿已禁止美国风险投资涉足某些中国先进技术领域。

In 2025, private A.I. investment in China totaled $12.4 billion, compared with $280 billion in the United States, according to the Stanford A.I. Index.

斯坦福人工智能指数显示，2025年中国私人人工智能投资总额为124亿美元，而美国为2800亿美元。

Han Lin, the China country director for the Asia Group, an advisory firm, said China had exceptional engineering talent and a government capable of mobilizing enormous resources for strategic industries.

咨询公司亚洲集团中国区总裁林汉昇(Han Lin)表示，中国拥有卓越的工程人才，以及一个能够为战略性产业调动庞大资源的政府。

But he added, “What frontier technology also needs is harder to mobilize — risk capital that can absorb failure.”

但他补充道：“前沿技术同样需要的东西却更难调动——能够承受失败的风险资本。”

据一份梁文锋对投资者讲话的文字记录，这位DeepSeek首席执行官表示，该公司需要四倍数量的华为芯片，才能匹配单颗先进英伟达芯片的性能。

Even the public markets, a lifeline for cash-hungry start-ups, are becoming less welcoming. Amid the sell-off, the Chinese authorities have instructed some companies to delay or suspend planned public listings, according to Cailian Press, a Chinese business publication, suggesting Beijing is concerned about an A.I. investment bubble.

就连作为渴望资金的初创企业生命线的公开市场也正变得不那么友好。据中国财经媒体财联社报道，在市场抛售潮中，中国当局已指示部分企业推迟或暂停原定的公开上市计划，这表明北京对人工智能投资泡沫感到担忧。

China has announced investment funds to support A.I., but much of the money has gone toward semiconductors rather than companies developing large language models.

中国已宣布设立支持人工智能的投资基金，但大部分资金流向了半导体领域，而非开发大语言模型的企业。

Government investors face many of the same constraints as private ones. Wang Renxuan, an assistant finance professor at the China Europe International Business School in Shanghai, said government funds also need a credible path to returns.

政府投资者面临着与私人投资者许多相同的制约。上海中欧国际工商学院金融学助理教授王任轩表示，政府基金同样需要一条可靠的回报路径。

Erik Walenza, a Shanghai-based managing partner at Asia Growth Partners, a consultancy advising on A.I., said it was difficult to see how Chinese A.I. companies could make their finances work “without a lot of sustained government financing.”

驻上海的人工智能咨询公司亚洲增长合伙人(Asia Growth Partners)管理合伙人埃里克·瓦伦扎表示，很难想象中国人工智能企业“在没有大量持续政府融资的情况下”如何实现财务运转。

The challenge, he added, is not only whether Chinese engineers can build models to rival America’s but also how much of the financial burden the government is prepared to shoulder.

他补充说，挑战不仅在于中国工程师能否构建出与美国相匹敌的模型，还在于政府准备承担多大的财政负担。

“It becomes more of a political will question, of how much sacrifice are we willing to make to compete in this area,” Mr. Walenza said.

“这更多变成了一个政治意愿问题，即我们愿意做出多大牺牲来在这一领域展开竞争，”瓦伦扎说。

黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)是《纽约时报》亚洲商业记者。

Li You是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，报道中国经济和商业新闻。
