Chinese A.I. labs have found costly workarounds, including renting data centers in Southeast Asia equipped with Nvidia chips. The Trump administration said this week it was moving forward with new rules to close that loophole.
关于中国在人工智能领域竞争能力的讨论，大多集中在美国为限制中国获取先进半导体而实施的出口管制上。中国的人工智能实验室已找到代价高昂的变通办法，包括在东南亚租赁配备英伟达芯片的数据中心。特朗普政府本周表示，正推进出台新规以堵住这一漏洞。

But money might prove an equally formidable obstacle. Even if Chinese companies can find the chips they need, they must raise enough capital to buy them and finance the rising cost of developing frontier models.
但资金可能成为同样难以逾越的障碍。即便中国企业能够找到所需的芯片，它们也必须筹集足够资金来购买芯片，并支撑开发前沿模型不断攀升的成本。
中国人工智能企业面临不断攀升的成本，既要获取先进芯片，又要为开发日益精密的模型提供资金。
Logan Wright, a partner at Rhodium Group who co-wrote a report on China’s A.I. financing, said those financial constraints “will be probably more decisive” than the chip shortage in the long term.
曾合著一份关于中国人工智能融资报告的荣鼎集团合伙人洛根·赖特表示，从长远来看，这些资金限制“可能比芯片短缺更具决定性”。
“The big problem is that the revenue mismatch with the Chinese models relative to capex is arguably more extreme than the U.S. case,” Mr. Wright said.
“最大的问题在于，中国模型相对于资本支出的收入错配，可以说比美国的情况更为极端，”赖特说。

American A.I. companies spend roughly five to six times what their Chinese counterparts do, but bring in substantially more money. China’s six leading A.I. firms collectively generate about one-tenth the combined revenue of OpenAI and Anthropic, according to Epoch AI, a nonprofit research organization.
美国人工智能企业的支出大约是中国同行的五到六倍，但带来的收入却要高得多。非营利研究机构Epoch AI的数据显示，中国六家领先人工智能企业的总收入，大约仅为OpenAI和Anthropic合并收入的十分之一。
China’s embrace of open-source A.I. has made that imbalance even harder to overcome.
中国对开源人工智能的拥抱，使这种失衡变得更加难以克服。

By allowing developers to use and modify their models freely, Chinese companies have accelerated the global spread of their technology. But that strategy has also undermined their ability to profit from it. Companies can charge for access, only to see rivals offer the same technology at lower prices. Fierce price wars have squeezed profits further.
通过允许开发者自由使用和修改其模型，中国企业加速了自身技术的全球传播。但这一策略也削弱了它们从中盈利的能力。企业一旦对访问收费，就会看到竞争对手以更低价格提供相同技术。激烈的价格战进一步挤压了利润。

Z.ai, a Chinese A.I. start-up, learned that lesson in August when it released its latest open-source model, GLM-5.3 Flash. The company halved prices for two weeks to entice users to run the model on Z.ai’s servers rather than their own. But competitors quickly moved in.
中国人工智能初创企业智谱(Z.ai)在8月发布其最新开源模型GLM-5.3 Flash时就尝到了这一教训。该公司将价格减半两周，以吸引用户在智谱的服务器而非自建服务器上运行该模型。但竞争对手迅速跟进。
By November, roughly 20 rival providers were charging less than Z.ai for access to its own technology, according to Open Router, a platform connecting users with A.I. models.
连接用户与人工智能模型的平台Open Router的数据显示，到11月，约有20家竞争对手服务商对智谱自身技术的访问收费低于智谱。
“Your own pricing power is lost during this process,” said Cheryl Wu, a researcher at GovAI, a think tank.
“在这一过程中，你自身的定价权丧失了，”智库GovAI研究员谢丽尔·吴表示。
“No one has figured out how to make money off consumers,” said Rui Ma, a technology investor, referring to Chinese A.I. start-ups.
“还没有人想明白如何从消费者身上赚钱，”科技投资者马睿在谈及中国人工智能初创企业时说。
The Cost of Compute
算力成本
Another obstacle worsens China’s financing problems: access to advanced Nvidia chips, the gold standard for training the most powerful A.I. models.
另一个障碍加剧了中国的融资难题：获取用于训练最强大人工智能模型的黄金标准——先进英伟达芯片。

From 2022 to June 2026, American companies possessed computing capacity equivalent to about 20 million Nvidia H100 chips, compared with roughly 2.6 million in China, some of it acquired through smuggling, according to EpochAI.
Epoch AI的数据显示，从2022年到2026年6月，美国企业拥有的算力相当于约2000万块英伟达H100芯片，而中国约为260万块，其中部分通过走私获得。

On Goofish, a Chinese secondhand online marketplace, sellers have advertised Nvidia’s DGX B300, an A.I. supercomputing server, for nearly $3 million — about eight times the U.S. price. Asking prices have reportedly quintupled since the start of the year, underscoring the premium Chinese companies must pay for advanced computing power.
在中国二手在线交易平台闲鱼上，卖家将人工智能超级计算服务器英伟达DGX B300标价近300万美元——约为美国价格的八倍。据报道，自年初以来要价已翻了五倍，凸显出中国企业为获取先进算力必须支付的高昂溢价。

The squeeze could worsen. Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief last week amid an investigation into a romantic relationship with a Chinese businesswoman, was a powerful advocate of doing business with China. On Tuesday, Nvidia said it would stop shipping its chips to China, a deal that President Trump had previously permitted at Mr. Huang’s urging. The company also said it had established an export control oversight committee.
这种挤压可能会进一步恶化。黄仁勋曾是对华开展业务的有力倡导者。他因与一名中国女商人的婚外情接受调查而于上周辞去英伟达首席执行官职务。（黄仁勋目前已复职——编注）周二，英伟达表示将停止向中国运送芯片，而这笔交易此前是在黄仁勋的敦促下获得特朗普总统批准的。该公司还表示已成立一个出口管制监督委员会。
2022年展示的英伟达H100图形处理器，专为处理大型人工智能模型而打造。

To reduce their dependence on American technology, Chinese developers are adapting their systems to run on chips made by Huawei, the Chinese telecommunications and electronics company leading the country’s chip charge.
为减少对美国技术的依赖，中国开发者正在调整其系统，使其能够在引领中国芯片攻关的电信和电子巨头华为制造的芯片上运行。

Liang Wenfeng, chief executive of DeepSeek, the Chinese start-up that stunned Silicon Valley by developing a powerful A.I. model at a fraction of the expected cost, said Huawei’s technology is only about two years behind Nvidia’s.
中国初创企业DeepSeek曾以远远低于预期的成本开发出强大人工智能模型，从而震惊硅谷，其首席执行官梁文锋表示，华为的技术仅落后英伟达约两年。

But the gap remains consequential. DeepSeek would need four times as many Huawei 950 chips to match the performance of a single advanced Nvidia GB300 chip, Mr. Liang said, according to a leaked transcript of his call with investors, excerpts from which Chinese media outlets published. Huawei also lacks sufficient production capacity, he added.
但差距依然显著。据一份泄露的梁文锋与投资者电话会议记录（中国媒体刊发了节选），他表示，DeepSeek需要四倍数量的华为950芯片才能匹配单颗先进英伟达GB300芯片的性能。他补充说，华为还缺乏足够的产能。
“We simply can’t afford to train the largest models available right now,” he said. DeepSeek did not respond to a request for comment.
“我们目前根本负担不起训练现有最大规模模型的费用，”他说。DeepSeek未回应置评请求。

Yet China’s A.I. industry has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to do more with less. Chinese researchers have pioneered techniques to train and run powerful models more efficiently. Silicon Valley has accused Chinese firms of copying leading American technologies through a process called distillation, reducing the time needed to build foundational models with expensive computing infrastructure.
然而，中国人工智能行业一再展现出以少胜多的能力。中国研究人员开创了更高效地训练和运行强大模型的技术。硅谷指责中国企业通过一种名为蒸馏的工艺抄袭美国领先技术，从而减少了利用昂贵计算基础设施构建基础模型所需的时间。
中国开发者正在调整系统，使其在华为芯片上运行，以减少对美国技术的依赖。
Worries of a Bubble
泡沫担忧
For China’s A.I. companies, finding investors willing to bankroll the competition is increasingly difficult.
对中国人工智能企业而言，寻找愿意为这场竞赛提供资金的投资者正变得越来越困难。

DeepSeek, which has raised more than $20 billion, is preparing for an initial public offering in Shanghai early next year, according to Chinese media reports. Its investors include Tencent, the battery maker CATL and state-backed investment funds.
据中国媒体报道，已融资逾200亿美元的DeepSeek正筹备明年初在上海进行首次公开募股。其投资者包括腾讯、电池制造商宁德时代以及国家背景的投资基金。
Few competitors have access to such deep pockets.
很少有竞争对手拥有如此雄厚的财力。

China’s venture capital industry has been shrinking since 2021 and though it has recovered slightly in the third quarter, it is still a fraction of its American counterpart. Banks are lending to China’s tech giants, but they are more cautious with smaller A.I. labs. Credit growth has fallen to historic lows, and the central bank governor has called for slower, “higher-quality” lending.
中国风险投资行业自2021年以来一直在萎缩，尽管第三季度略有回升，但仍只是美国同行的一个零头。银行正在向中国科技巨头放贷，但对规模较小的人工智能实验室则更为谨慎。信贷增速已降至历史低点，央行行长也呼吁放缓步伐、开展“更高质量”的信贷投放。

Foreign investment has also dried up. U.S. dollar-denominated investment funds in China have plunged partly because Washington has barred American venture capital from certain advanced Chinese technologies.
外国投资也已枯竭。在华美元计价投资基金大幅缩水，部分原因是华盛顿已禁止美国风险投资涉足某些中国先进技术领域。
In 2025, private A.I. investment in China totaled $12.4 billion, compared with $280 billion in the United States, according to the Stanford A.I. Index.
斯坦福人工智能指数显示，2025年中国私人人工智能投资总额为124亿美元，而美国为2800亿美元。

Han Lin, the China country director for the Asia Group, an advisory firm, said China had exceptional engineering talent and a government capable of mobilizing enormous resources for strategic industries.
咨询公司亚洲集团中国区总裁林汉昇(Han Lin)表示，中国拥有卓越的工程人才，以及一个能够为战略性产业调动庞大资源的政府。
But he added, “What frontier technology also needs is harder to mobilize — risk capital that can absorb failure.”
但他补充道：“前沿技术同样需要的东西却更难调动——能够承受失败的风险资本。”
据一份梁文锋对投资者讲话的文字记录，这位DeepSeek首席执行官表示，该公司需要四倍数量的华为芯片，才能匹配单颗先进英伟达芯片的性能。

Even the public markets, a lifeline for cash-hungry start-ups, are becoming less welcoming. Amid the sell-off, the Chinese authorities have instructed some companies to delay or suspend planned public listings, according to Cailian Press, a Chinese business publication, suggesting Beijing is concerned about an A.I. investment bubble.
就连作为渴望资金的初创企业生命线的公开市场也正变得不那么友好。据中国财经媒体财联社报道，在市场抛售潮中，中国当局已指示部分企业推迟或暂停原定的公开上市计划，这表明北京对人工智能投资泡沫感到担忧。
China has announced investment funds to support A.I., but much of the money has gone toward semiconductors rather than companies developing large language models.
中国已宣布设立支持人工智能的投资基金，但大部分资金流向了半导体领域，而非开发大语言模型的企业。

Government investors face many of the same constraints as private ones. Wang Renxuan, an assistant finance professor at the China Europe International Business School in Shanghai, said government funds also need a credible path to returns.
政府投资者面临着与私人投资者许多相同的制约。上海中欧国际工商学院金融学助理教授王任轩表示，政府基金同样需要一条可靠的回报路径。

Erik Walenza, a Shanghai-based managing partner at Asia Growth Partners, a consultancy advising on A.I., said it was difficult to see how Chinese A.I. companies could make their finances work “without a lot of sustained government financing.”
驻上海的人工智能咨询公司亚洲增长合伙人(Asia Growth Partners)管理合伙人埃里克·瓦伦扎表示，很难想象中国人工智能企业“在没有大量持续政府融资的情况下”如何实现财务运转。
The challenge, he added, is not only whether Chinese engineers can build models to rival America’s but also how much of the financial burden the government is prepared to shoulder.
他补充说，挑战不仅在于中国工程师能否构建出与美国相匹敌的模型，还在于政府准备承担多大的财政负担。
“It becomes more of a political will question, of how much sacrifice are we willing to make to compete in this area,” Mr. Walenza said.
“这更多变成了一个政治意愿问题，即我们愿意做出多大牺牲来在这一领域展开竞争，”瓦伦扎说。
黄瑞黎(Sui-Lee Wee)是《纽约时报》亚洲商业记者。
Li You是《纽约时报》记者/研究员，报道中国经济和商业新闻。

items.body:
官方通报学生课间说四川话被认定违纪：责令校方立即废止不当规定

11月25日晚，四川宜宾市翠屏区教育和体育局发布情况通报：

近日，有网民反映棠湖学校在教育管理过程中存在失范相关问题。翠屏区教育和体育局高度重视，成立工作组到校开展专项核查。现将有关情况通报如下：

经核查，棠湖学校落实《国家通用语言文字法》相关规定，课堂坚持使用普通话，倡导师生在校内使用普通话，但在执行中存在管理方式机械化、简单化的问题。

经核查，棠湖学校按照《中学生日常行为规范》，对学生仪容仪表加强了管理，但在实际管理过程中存在教条生硬、方式不当的情况。
针对存在的问题，翠屏区教育和体育局对棠湖学校作出如下处理：

一是责令棠湖学校立即废止不当规定，严禁拍摄学生影像用于纪律管理，对已拍照片进行删除，相关类似情况不认定为违纪。二是约谈棠湖学校主要负责人，责令学校就教育管理问题作出深刻检查；依据《中小学教师违反职业道德行为处理办法》等规定，对相关教师予以通报批评、诫勉谈话。三是责令棠湖学校严格对照教育相关管理规定，对学校管理制度中不规范内容立即进行修订。

下一步，我局将举一反三，在全区学校开展排查，督促各学校依规治校，把握好教育管理的尺度和温度，切实保障学生合法权益。

items.title: 美国贸易代表办公室11月25日宣布对包括中国、欧盟、日本和印度在内的14个经济体加征关税。
items.summary: 美国贸易代表办公室称，依据《1974年贸易法》第301条认定，上述经济体关于制造业结构性产能过剩的行为、政策和做法不合理，对美国商业造成负担或限制。 对于某些中国商品，新的20%关税将叠加于其他关税之上，总税率将达到45%。越南也面临20%的税率，其他贸易伙伴的关税范围在10%到18%之间。 新的进口税针对特定产品，不会叠加在汽车和钢铁的其他现有关税之上。 中国外交部称，所谓“产能过剩”是一个伪命题，中方反对以此为借口进行政治操弄。 （CNBC，美联社，中国外交部）
items.body:
美国贸易代表办公室11月25日宣布对包括中国、欧盟、日本和印度在内的14个经济体加征关税。
美国贸易代表办公室称，依据《1974年贸易法》第301条认定，上述经济体关于制造业结构性产能过剩的行为、政策和做法不合理，对美国商业造成负担或限制。
对于某些中国商品，新的20%关税将叠加于其他关税之上，总税率将达到45%。越南也面临20%的税率，其他贸易伙伴的关税范围在10%到18%之间。
新的进口税针对特定产品，不会叠加在汽车和钢铁的其他现有关税之上。
中国外交部称，所谓“产能过剩”是一个伪命题，中方反对以此为借口进行政治操弄。
（CNBC，美联社，中国外交部）

quote.text: 美国国际贸易法院5月7日裁定，特朗普政府征收10%全球进口关税是非法的，超出国会赋予总统的关税权力。目前尚不清楚政府是否会提出上诉。 最高法院2月20日认定特朗普政府的“对等关税”逾越总统职权。特朗普随后发布行政令，临时施加10%全球进口关税，为期150天。随后华盛顿州政府和两家企业提起诉讼。 （美联社）

items.summary: 事发时，两人正在为船只加油和补给。 与国民代表大会结盟的“国民军”控制着该国的东部和南部，和俄罗斯关系密切。用于乌克兰无人机发射的利比亚西部则由民族统一政府及支持的武装团体控制。 乌克兰据报在西方认可的秘密协议下在利比亚西部行动，但民族统一政府否认与乌克兰达成协议，强调利比亚领土不能当作实施敌对行动的跳板。 （新华社，美联社）
items.body:
利比亚“国民军”11月24日晚称，两名“国民军”士兵在乌克兰对俄罗斯军舰的袭击中死亡，并誓言报复。事发时，两人正在为船只加油和补给。
与国民代表大会结盟的“国民军”控制着该国的东部和南部，和俄罗斯关系密切。用于乌克兰无人机发射的利比亚西部则由民族统一政府及支持的武装团体控制。
乌克兰据报在西方认可的秘密协议下在利比亚西部行动，但民族统一政府否认与乌克兰达成协议，强调利比亚领土不能当作实施敌对行动的跳板。
（新华社，美联社）

quote.text: 乌克兰11月22日使用7艘无人艇在利比亚沿海袭击了俄罗斯“水星”号护卫舰和一艘据称运输武器的干货船，并摧毁一架俄军卡-27直升机。 利比亚官员称，乌军根据西方认可的秘密协议在利比亚西部行动，其中大多人是无人机专家。 克里姆林宫拒绝对此事置评，仅表示俄国防部将在适当情况下提供更多信息。 （美联社）

items.title: 美国司法部：
items.summary: 中国科技巨头华为及其数家子公司被裁定以下罪名成立： 🔴 违反制裁 🔴 欺诈 🔴 串谋窃取商业秘密 🔴 洗钱 数十年来，被告方一直密谋暗中为伊朗政府提供协助，窃取美国企业的商业机密，欺骗美国银行和国会，并从事洗钱活动。 “没有谁能凌驾于法律之上，”美国司法部长托德·布兰奇说，“数十年来，华为及其三家子公司通过谎言和窃取的手段在美国开展业务。因为有联邦调查局和我们联邦检察官的努力，那些参与这些犯罪活动的人都将被追究责任。”
items.body:
美国司法部：

中国科技巨头华为及其数家子公司被裁定以下罪名成立：

🔴 违反制裁
🔴 欺诈
🔴 串谋窃取商业秘密
🔴 洗钱

数十年来，被告方一直密谋暗中为伊朗政府提供协助，窃取美国企业的商业机密，欺骗美国银行和国会，并从事洗钱活动。

“没有谁能凌驾于法律之上，”美国司法部长托德·布兰奇说，“数十年来，华为及其三家子公司通过谎言和窃取的手段在美国开展业务。因为有联邦调查局和我们联邦检察官的努力，那些参与这些犯罪活动的人都将被追究责任。”

items.title: 男子造谣华为鸿蒙被处罚
items.summary: 在网络传播高速化的当下，一条未经核实的言论、一段刻意编造的虚假视频，无需成本，却能在短时间内快速发酵传播，摧毁企业积攒多年的品牌口碑。 湖南网警聚焦涉企造谣抹黑类违法案件，今日公开了一起“恶意抹黑知名企业产品，散布数百条不实言论”典型案例： 2026 年以来，网民李某峰在多个主流短视频平台评论区，依托碎片化网络信息，在无任何权威依据、未经核实的前提下，针对华为手机、鸿蒙系统、问界汽车等知名产品，持续发布数百条不实评论，捏造“千亿营销费用”“研发费用造假”等虚假信息。 海量不实言论持续扩散，严重误导公众认知，对企业品牌形象造成极大负面影响，引发不良社会舆论。目前，公安机关已依法对其处以行政处罚。
items.body:
男子造谣华为鸿蒙被处罚

在网络传播高速化的当下，一条未经核实的言论、一段刻意编造的虚假视频，无需成本，却能在短时间内快速发酵传播，摧毁企业积攒多年的品牌口碑。

湖南网警聚焦涉企造谣抹黑类违法案件，今日公开了一起“恶意抹黑知名企业产品，散布数百条不实言论”典型案例：

2026 年以来，网民李某峰在多个主流短视频平台评论区，依托碎片化网络信息，在无任何权威依据、未经核实的前提下，针对华为手机、鸿蒙系统、问界汽车等知名产品，持续发布数百条不实评论，捏造“千亿营销费用”“研发费用造假”等虚假信息。

海量不实言论持续扩散，严重误导公众认知，对企业品牌形象造成极大负面影响，引发不良社会舆论。目前，公安机关已依法对其处以行政处罚。

items.summary: 华为在美被判窃取商业机密等罪名成立 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
SANTUL NERKAR, KATE CHRISTOBEK2026年11月25日

由于华为自2019年以来实际上已被禁止在美国销售产品，这一酝酿已久的裁决或许不会对其命运产生重大影响。 Greg Baker/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

A federal jury on Tuesday found Huawei, the Chinese telecommunications giant that U.S. officials have long viewed with suspicion, guilty of stealing trade secrets and evading sanctions against Iran.

周二，一个联邦陪审团裁定，长期受到美国官员怀疑的中国电信巨头华为窃取商业机密和规避对伊朗制裁的罪名成立。

The verdict, which came after an 11-week trial and nearly a week of deliberations in Federal District Court in Brooklyn, was a victory for the Justice Department in a long-running case over what federal prosecutors called systematic and brazen trade theft.

这一裁决是在布鲁克林联邦地区法院经过11周审理和近一周闭门商议后作出的，也是司法部在这起旷日持久案件中的一场胜利，联邦检察官称该案涉及系统性且公然的商业盗窃。

The allegations burst into international view in 2018, when a senior executive at Huawei, Meng Wanzhou, was detained by Canadian authorities at the direction of the U.S. government. Ms. Meng spent three years in detention at her luxurious Vancouver homes before reaching an agreement with federal prosecutors that allowed her to return to China.

相关指控于2018年进入国际视野，当时华为高管孟晚舟在美国政府指示下被加拿大当局拘留。孟晚舟在温哥华的豪宅中被拘禁了三年，随后与联邦检察官达成协议，得以返回中国。

But the U.S. government continued its prosecution, even without her as a defendant, accusing Huawei of acting like a criminal enterprise set on stealing secrets from American competitors.

但即使没有她作为被告，美国政府仍继续推进起诉，指控华为的运作如同一个致力于窃取美国竞争对手机密的犯罪集团。

Since Huawei has been effectively banned from selling its products in the United States since 2019, the long-awaited verdict may not significantly affect its fortunes. Still, a stiff financial penalty and the stain of a guilty judgment could hamper its business.

由于华为自2019年以来实际上已被禁止在美国销售产品，这一酝酿已久的裁决或许不会对其命运产生重大影响。不过，高额罚款以及有罪判决的污点仍可能阻碍其业务发展。

Huawei has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has rejected the allegation that it has operated at the behest of the Chinese Communist Party.

华为始终否认有任何不当行为，并驳斥了其听命于中国共产党的指控。

The company was found guilty of 10 of the dozen criminal counts it faced, which included bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.

该公司面临的12项刑事指控中有10项被裁定罪名成立，其中包括银行欺诈、串谋窃取商业机密以及串谋欺诈美国。

But jurors acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy, a result that undercut the Justice Department’s central claim that the company operated as a criminal enterprise. The company was also acquitted of conspiring to obstruct justice.

但陪审员裁定华为勒索敲诈共谋罪名不成立，这一结果削弱了司法部关于该公司作为犯罪集团运作的核心主张。该公司串谋妨碍司法公正的罪名也被裁定不成立。

“Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws,” Joseph Nocella Jr., the U.S. attorney in Brooklyn, said in a statement.

“以华为数十年来危害美国国家安全、侵犯美国商业神圣性以及阻碍美国法律执行的行为模式，罪行之深重实属罕见，”布鲁克林联邦检察官小约瑟夫·诺塞拉在一份声明中表示。

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, told reporters outside the courthouse that the company’s acquittal on the racketeering charge showed a “profound rejection of the United States’ narratives about what Huawei is.” He said he expected the company would appeal the guilty verdicts.

华为律师布赖恩·赫伯利格在法院外对记者表示，该公司勒索敲诈罪名不成立表明，陪审团“彻底否定了美国关于华为性质的叙事”。他表示预计公司将对有罪裁决提出上诉。

“The allegations that the government made in this case overreached and simply weren’t consistent with the successful, innovative and hard-working company that we came to know and deeply respect in this trial,” Mr. Heberlig said.

“政府在本案中提出的指控过于牵强，根本不符合我们在这次审判中所认识并深感敬佩的这家成功、创新且勤奋的公司，”赫伯利格说。

Over the course of the trial, which began in September, federal prosecutors in Brooklyn painted a portrait of a company that endeavored to cheat American firms out of their intellectual property.

在9月开始的审判过程中，布鲁克林的联邦检察官将华为描绘成一家竭力骗取美国企业知识产权的公司。

Leaders at Huawei, prosecutors said, encouraged employees to steal secrets. Prosecutors said that Huawei stole intellectual property from T-Mobile and Cisco, among other companies.

检察官称，华为领导层鼓励员工窃取机密。检察官表示，华为窃取了包括T-Mobile和思科在内的多家公司的知识产权。

Huawei’s backers have argued for years that the case was politically motivated and a retaliation against a Chinese initiative to build 5G networks around the world.

多年来，华为的支持者一直认为此案具有政治动机，是对中国在全球建设5G网络倡议的报复。

Mr. Heberlig said in his closing statement that Huawei was “a global company that built its success through innovation and hard work.” The company, he said, did not steal technology; instead, it asked for it and paid for it.

赫伯利格在结案陈词中表示，华为是“一家通过创新和辛勤工作取得成功的全球性公司”。他说，该公司没有窃取技术，而是提出申请并支付了费用。

“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success; it earned it,” Mr. Heberlig said. “Plain and simple.”

“华为不是靠偷窃走向成功的；它是靠实力赢得的，”赫伯利格说。“就这么简单。”

Meredith Arfa, a federal prosecutor, told the jury in her closing statement that employees had been ordered to collect competitor information and had even been paid bonuses for their crimes.

联邦检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法在结案陈词中告诉陪审团，华为员工曾奉命收集竞争对手的信息，甚至因犯罪行为获得奖金。

“For 20 years, Huawei committed a pattern of crimes targeted at American companies, the American financial system and the American government,” Ms. Arfa said.

“20年来，华为实施了一系列针对美国企业、美国金融体系和美国政府的犯罪活动，”阿尔法说。

In addition, prosecutors said, the company evaded U.S. sanctions by conducting business in Iran, where it sold gear that allowed the authoritarian government to surveil its citizens. Huawei, prosecutors said, lied to banks and to the news media about its business in Iran.

此外，检察官称，该公司在伊朗开展业务规避了美国制裁，在当地销售允许这个威权政府监控其公民的设备。检察官表示，华为在伊朗业务问题上向银行和新闻媒体撒谎。

At trade shows, Huawei engineers would sneak photographs of other companies’ hardware, including their routers and internal circuitry, according to witness testimony. A former employee at a Huawei subsidiary testified that the company’s employees would intentionally get “lost in competitors’ facilities and end up in places they weren’t supposed to be.”

根据证人证词，在贸易展会上，华为工程师会偷拍其他公司的硬件，包括路由器和内部电路。华为一家子公司的一名前员工作证称，该公司员工会故意在“竞争对手的设施中迷路，最终出现在他们本不该出现的地方”。

A testing robot that belonged to T-Mobile, known as “Tappy,” was another target of Huawei’s illicit schemes, prosecutors said at trial. In 2012, T-Mobile allowed Huawei to use the robot so that Huawei could test its own phones. But in reality, prosecutors said, Huawei used its access to steal technical information about the robot, which the company then passed along to its research and development team in China.

检察官在庭审中表示，T-Mobile一款名为“Tappy”的测试机器人是华为非法计划的另一个目标。2012年，T-Mobile允许华为使用该机器人，以便华为测试自家手机。但检察官称，实际上华为利用这一权限窃取了该机器人的技术信息，随后将其传送给在中国的研发团队。

Mr. Heberlig dismissed the theft of trade secrets as “isolated misconduct by company employees,” which he said was impossible to prevent at a company that employed hundreds of thousands of people.

赫伯利格将窃取商业机密的行为淡化为“公司员工的孤立不当行为”，并称在一家拥有数十万名员工的公司里，这种行为无法完全杜绝。

Huawei was founded in the 1980s by Ren Zhengfei, Ms. Meng’s father. Its own rise mirrored that of China, as it transitioned toward capitalism and a market economy.

华为由孟晚舟的父亲任正非于20世纪80年代创立。随着中国向资本主义和市场经济转型，华为自身的崛起也折射出中国的发展轨迹。

The company’s ascent worried some U.S. officials, who said that its technology could be used to spy on American citizens. Officials also accused the company of dodging U.S. laws against doing business with Iran.

该公司的崛起令一些美国官员感到担忧，他们称其技术可能被用来监视美国公民。官员们还指责该公司规避美国禁止与伊朗开展业务的法律。

In the years since the prosecution began, Huawei has become a crucial part of China’s development of artificial intelligence chips, creating an alternative to American technology in a race for global A.I. hegemony.

自起诉开始以来的几年里，华为已成为中国人工智能芯片研发的关键组成部分，在争夺全球人工智能霸权的竞赛中打造出美国技术的替代方案。

Since the Huawei case was first brought, the Justice Department’s focus on China has evolved alongside shifts in the global economy. The department announced last week that it was pursuing a criminal investigation into allegations that Megaspeed, a Singaporean company, was smuggling A.I. chips into China.

自华为案首次提起诉讼以来，司法部对中国的关注点也随着全球经济的变化而演变。该部门上周宣布，正对新加坡公司Megaspeed涉嫌向中国走私人工智能芯片的指控展开刑事调查。

Megaspeed had been led by Alice Huang, who U.S. officials believed worked as an asset for Chinese intelligence and who had an affair with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia.

Megaspeed此前由黄乐(Alice Huang)领导，美国官员认为她曾为中国情报部门线人，并与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有过婚外情。

When the criminal case against Huawei began in 2018, the United States and China were locked in a trade war started by President Trump. Mr. Trump, then in his first term, mused that he could get involved with Ms. Meng’s case to help secure a potential trade deal.

2018年针对华为的刑事诉讼启动时，美中正陷入由特朗普总统挑起的贸易战。当时处于第一任期的特朗普曾考虑介入孟晚舟的案件，以利潜在贸易协议的达成。

Under the agreement Ms. Meng reached, she admitted that Huawei had misled a bank about the company’s dealings with Iran. In 2021, Ms. Meng was welcomed back as a hero in China, where she remains the company’s chief financial officer.

根据孟晚舟达成的协议，她承认华为就公司在伊朗的业务误导了一家银行。2021年，回到中国的孟晚舟得到英雄般的欢迎，目前她仍担任该公司首席财务官。

“Meng committed crimes on Huawei’s behalf, and then Huawei put her in charge,” Ms. Arfa said in her closing statement. “That’s not a company that prohibits criminal conduct. That is a company that encourages it, demands it, rewards it.”

“孟晚舟代表华为实施了犯罪，而华为随后让她掌管大权，”阿尔法在结案陈词中说。“这不是一家禁止犯罪行为的公司，而是一家鼓励、要求并奖励犯罪的公司。”

Santul Nerkar是《纽约时报》记者，报道布鲁克林联邦法院新闻。

Kate Christobek是《纽约时报》记者，报道突发新闻。

周二，一个联邦陪审团裁定，长期受到美国官员怀疑的中国电信巨头华为窃取商业机密和规避对伊朗制裁的罪名成立。

The verdict, which came after an 11-week trial and nearly a week of deliberations in Federal District Court in Brooklyn, was a victory for the Justice Department in a long-running case over what federal prosecutors called systematic and brazen trade theft.
这一裁决是在布鲁克林联邦地区法院经过11周审理和近一周闭门商议后作出的，也是司法部在这起旷日持久案件中的一场胜利，联邦检察官称该案涉及系统性且公然的商业盗窃。

The allegations burst into international view in 2018, when a senior executive at Huawei, Meng Wanzhou, was detained by Canadian authorities at the direction of the U.S. government. Ms. Meng spent three years in detention at her luxurious Vancouver homes before reaching an agreement with federal prosecutors that allowed her to return to China.
相关指控于2018年进入国际视野，当时华为高管孟晚舟在美国政府指示下被加拿大当局拘留。孟晚舟在温哥华的豪宅中被拘禁了三年，随后与联邦检察官达成协议，得以返回中国。
But the U.S. government continued its prosecution, even without her as a defendant, accusing Huawei of acting like a criminal enterprise set on stealing secrets from American competitors.
但即使没有她作为被告，美国政府仍继续推进起诉，指控华为的运作如同一个致力于窃取美国竞争对手机密的犯罪集团。

Since Huawei has been effectively banned from selling its products in the United States since 2019, the long-awaited verdict may not significantly affect its fortunes. Still, a stiff financial penalty and the stain of a guilty judgment could hamper its business.
由于华为自2019年以来实际上已被禁止在美国销售产品，这一酝酿已久的裁决或许不会对其命运产生重大影响。不过，高额罚款以及有罪判决的污点仍可能阻碍其业务发展。
Huawei has consistently denied any wrongdoing and has rejected the allegation that it has operated at the behest of the Chinese Communist Party.
华为始终否认有任何不当行为，并驳斥了其听命于中国共产党的指控。
The company was found guilty of 10 of the dozen criminal counts it faced, which included bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States.
该公司面临的12项刑事指控中有10项被裁定罪名成立，其中包括银行欺诈、串谋窃取商业机密以及串谋欺诈美国。

But jurors acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy, a result that undercut the Justice Department’s central claim that the company operated as a criminal enterprise. The company was also acquitted of conspiring to obstruct justice.
但陪审员裁定华为勒索敲诈共谋罪名不成立，这一结果削弱了司法部关于该公司作为犯罪集团运作的核心主张。该公司串谋妨碍司法公正的罪名也被裁定不成立。

“Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws,” Joseph Nocella Jr., the U.S. attorney in Brooklyn, said in a statement.
“以华为数十年来危害美国国家安全、侵犯美国商业神圣性以及阻碍美国法律执行的行为模式，罪行之深重实属罕见，”布鲁克林联邦检察官小约瑟夫·诺塞拉在一份声明中表示。

Brian Heberlig, a lawyer for Huawei, told reporters outside the courthouse that the company’s acquittal on the racketeering charge showed a “profound rejection of the United States’ narratives about what Huawei is.” He said he expected the company would appeal the guilty verdicts.
华为律师布赖恩·赫伯利格在法院外对记者表示，该公司勒索敲诈罪名不成立表明，陪审团“彻底否定了美国关于华为性质的叙事”。他表示预计公司将对有罪裁决提出上诉。

“The allegations that the government made in this case overreached and simply weren’t consistent with the successful, innovative and hard-working company that we came to know and deeply respect in this trial,” Mr. Heberlig said.
“政府在本案中提出的指控过于牵强，根本不符合我们在这次审判中所认识并深感敬佩的这家成功、创新且勤奋的公司，”赫伯利格说。
Over the course of the trial, which began in September, federal prosecutors in Brooklyn painted a portrait of a company that endeavored to cheat American firms out of their intellectual property.
在9月开始的审判过程中，布鲁克林的联邦检察官将华为描绘成一家竭力骗取美国企业知识产权的公司。
Leaders at Huawei, prosecutors said, encouraged employees to steal secrets. Prosecutors said that Huawei stole intellectual property from T-Mobile and Cisco, among other companies.
检察官称，华为领导层鼓励员工窃取机密。检察官表示，华为窃取了包括T-Mobile和思科在内的多家公司的知识产权。
Huawei’s backers have argued for years that the case was politically motivated and a retaliation against a Chinese initiative to build 5G networks around the world.
多年来，华为的支持者一直认为此案具有政治动机，是对中国在全球建设5G网络倡议的报复。

Mr. Heberlig said in his closing statement that Huawei was “a global company that built its success through innovation and hard work.” The company, he said, did not steal technology; instead, it asked for it and paid for it.
赫伯利格在结案陈词中表示，华为是“一家通过创新和辛勤工作取得成功的全球性公司”。他说，该公司没有窃取技术，而是提出申请并支付了费用。
“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success; it earned it,” Mr. Heberlig said. “Plain and simple.”
“华为不是靠偷窃走向成功的；它是靠实力赢得的，”赫伯利格说。“就这么简单。”
Meredith Arfa, a federal prosecutor, told the jury in her closing statement that employees had been ordered to collect competitor information and had even been paid bonuses for their crimes.
联邦检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法在结案陈词中告诉陪审团，华为员工曾奉命收集竞争对手的信息，甚至因犯罪行为获得奖金。
“For 20 years, Huawei committed a pattern of crimes targeted at American companies, the American financial system and the American government,” Ms. Arfa said.
“20年来，华为实施了一系列针对美国企业、美国金融体系和美国政府的犯罪活动，”阿尔法说。

In addition, prosecutors said, the company evaded U.S. sanctions by conducting business in Iran, where it sold gear that allowed the authoritarian government to surveil its citizens. Huawei, prosecutors said, lied to banks and to the news media about its business in Iran.
此外，检察官称，该公司在伊朗开展业务规避了美国制裁，在当地销售允许这个威权政府监控其公民的设备。检察官表示，华为在伊朗业务问题上向银行和新闻媒体撒谎。

At trade shows, Huawei engineers would sneak photographs of other companies’ hardware, including their routers and internal circuitry, according to witness testimony. A former employee at a Huawei subsidiary testified that the company’s employees would intentionally get “lost in competitors’ facilities and end up in places they weren’t supposed to be.”
根据证人证词，在贸易展会上，华为工程师会偷拍其他公司的硬件，包括路由器和内部电路。华为一家子公司的一名前员工作证称，该公司员工会故意在“竞争对手的设施中迷路，最终出现在他们本不该出现的地方”。

A testing robot that belonged to T-Mobile, known as “Tappy,” was another target of Huawei’s illicit schemes, prosecutors said at trial. In 2012, T-Mobile allowed Huawei to use the robot so that Huawei could test its own phones. But in reality, prosecutors said, Huawei used its access to steal technical information about the robot, which the company then passed along to its research and development team in China.
检察官在庭审中表示，T-Mobile一款名为“Tappy”的测试机器人是华为非法计划的另一个目标。2012年，T-Mobile允许华为使用该机器人，以便华为测试自家手机。但检察官称，实际上华为利用这一权限窃取了该机器人的技术信息，随后将其传送给在中国的研发团队。
Mr. Heberlig dismissed the theft of trade secrets as “isolated misconduct by company employees,” which he said was impossible to prevent at a company that employed hundreds of thousands of people.
赫伯利格将窃取商业机密的行为淡化为“公司员工的孤立不当行为”，并称在一家拥有数十万名员工的公司里，这种行为无法完全杜绝。
Huawei was founded in the 1980s by Ren Zhengfei, Ms. Meng’s father. Its own rise mirrored that of China, as it transitioned toward capitalism and a market economy.
华为由孟晚舟的父亲任正非于20世纪80年代创立。随着中国向资本主义和市场经济转型，华为自身的崛起也折射出中国的发展轨迹。

The company’s ascent worried some U.S. officials, who said that its technology could be used to spy on American citizens. Officials also accused the company of dodging U.S. laws against doing business with Iran.
该公司的崛起令一些美国官员感到担忧，他们称其技术可能被用来监视美国公民。官员们还指责该公司规避美国禁止与伊朗开展业务的法律。

In the years since the prosecution began, Huawei has become a crucial part of China’s development of artificial intelligence chips, creating an alternative to American technology in a race for global A.I. hegemony.
自起诉开始以来的几年里，华为已成为中国人工智能芯片研发的关键组成部分，在争夺全球人工智能霸权的竞赛中打造出美国技术的替代方案。

Since the Huawei case was first brought, the Justice Department’s focus on China has evolved alongside shifts in the global economy. The department announced last week that it was pursuing a criminal investigation into allegations that Megaspeed, a Singaporean company, was smuggling A.I. chips into China.
自华为案首次提起诉讼以来，司法部对中国的关注点也随着全球经济的变化而演变。该部门上周宣布，正对新加坡公司Megaspeed涉嫌向中国走私人工智能芯片的指控展开刑事调查。
Megaspeed had been led by Alice Huang, who U.S. officials believed worked as an asset for Chinese intelligence and who had an affair with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia.
Megaspeed此前由黄乐(Alice Huang)领导，美国官员认为她曾为中国情报部门线人，并与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有过婚外情。

When the criminal case against Huawei began in 2018, the United States and China were locked in a trade war started by President Trump. Mr. Trump, then in his first term, mused that he could get involved with Ms. Meng’s case to help secure a potential trade deal.
2018年针对华为的刑事诉讼启动时，美中正陷入由特朗普总统挑起的贸易战。当时处于第一任期的特朗普曾考虑介入孟晚舟的案件，以利潜在贸易协议的达成。

Under the agreement Ms. Meng reached, she admitted that Huawei had misled a bank about the company’s dealings with Iran. In 2021, Ms. Meng was welcomed back as a hero in China, where she remains the company’s chief financial officer.
根据孟晚舟达成的协议，她承认华为就公司在伊朗的业务误导了一家银行。2021年，回到中国的孟晚舟得到英雄般的欢迎，目前她仍担任该公司首席财务官。

“Meng committed crimes on Huawei’s behalf, and then Huawei put her in charge,” Ms. Arfa said in her closing statement. “That’s not a company that prohibits criminal conduct. That is a company that encourages it, demands it, rewards it.”
“孟晚舟代表华为实施了犯罪，而华为随后让她掌管大权，”阿尔法在结案陈词中说。“这不是一家禁止犯罪行为的公司，而是一家鼓励、要求并奖励犯罪的公司。”
Santul Nerkar是《纽约时报》记者，报道布鲁克林联邦法院新闻。
Kate Christobek是《纽约时报》记者，报道突发新闻。

items.summary: 为什么黄仁勋不可撼动 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
STEPHEN WITT2026年11月25日

Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

When Jensen Huang returned to the floor of his Silicon Valley headquarters on Monday, his employees greeted him with a standing ovation. The rank and file of Nvidia love Mr. Huang, who has made many of them wealthy. In the midst of this celebration, I imagine his top executives must have exchanged a few glances. They know all about Mr. Huang’s abusive treatment of staff members, his extramarital relationships and Nvidia’s funny business in Southeast Asia. But, in the end, I’m sure they clapped, too.

周一，黄仁勋回到英伟达位于硅谷的总部时，员工们起立鼓掌欢迎。英伟达的普通员工都很爱戴黄仁勋，他让许多人赚得盆满钵满。在这欢庆的场面中，我想公司的高管们一定交换了几下眼神。他们对黄仁勋粗暴对待员工的行为、他的婚外情以及英伟达在东南亚那些见不得光的生意都心知肚明。不过，我相信最后他们也鼓掌了。

In the 11 days he was gone, Nvidia lost almost 30 percent of its value. Upon his return, Nvidia’s stock price recovered, adding almost a trillion dollars to the company’s market capitalization. They’re saying Jensen Huang is too big to fire. I say he’s the trillion-dollar man.

在他离开的11天里，英伟达市值损失近30%。他回归后，英伟达股价回升，公司市值增加近1万亿美元。人们说，黄仁勋重要到不能解雇。要我说，他是个价值万亿美元的男人。

Mr. Huang still has a number of looming scandals. Nvidia is being investigated by Congress, the Justice Department, the Securities and Exchange Commission and its own corporate board. The U.S. intelligence community seems to have compromising intelligence on Mr. Huang; he’s reportedly had numerous affairs, including one with a married corporate executive at his company and another with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

黄仁勋仍有多桩丑闻悬而未决。英伟达正受到国会、司法部、证券交易委员会及其自身董事会的调查。美国情报界似乎掌握了足以让黄仁勋陷入被动的情报；据报道，他有多次婚外情，包括与公司一名已婚女高管，以及与一名疑似中国间谍的女子。

Reporters have produced detailed accounts of his scathing encounters with staff members, which include bodily threats and ritual humiliation. He is scheduled to have a closed-door interview with House committees next Tuesday and to testify before the Senate two days later. For another corporate executive, any one of these scandals would be a career-killer. For Mr. Huang, it’s Monday morning.

记者们详细披露了他如何刻薄地对待员工，其中包括人身威胁和仪式化的羞辱。他定于下周二接受众议院多个委员会的闭门问询，并于两天后赴参议院作证。换作其他企业高管，这些丑闻中的任何一桩都足以断送职业生涯。对黄仁勋而言，这不过是一个寻常的周一早晨。

Mr. Huang’s invincibility derives from his close relationship with President Trump. Mr. Huang started cultivating this connection in 2025, when he and his wife, Lori, visited Mar-a-Lago. There, over dinner, he told Mr. Trump the compelling story of his rise from Denny’s waitstaff to semiconductor chief executive. In the course of writing Mr. Huang’s biography, I heard him tell this story many times. I never got tired of it — although I did notice the details change a bit at different tellings. The dazzled Mr. Trump fell hard for Mr. Huang. He also fell for Lori, whom on Monday he called a “fantastic woman” and “very supportive.”

黄仁勋之所以不可撼动，源于他与特朗普总统的密切关系。2025年，黄仁勋和妻子洛丽到访马阿拉歌庄园，从那时起，他便开始经营这段关系。席间，他向特朗普讲述了自己如何从连锁餐厅Denny's的一名服务员成长为半导体企业首席执行官的动人故事。在为黄仁勋撰写传记的过程中，我多次听他讲过这个故事，始终百听不厌——尽管我确实注意到，每次讲述的细节略有不同。听得入迷的特朗普彻底被黄仁勋征服了。他也很喜欢洛丽，周一还称她是个“了不起的女人”，对丈夫“非常支持”。

By the beginning of this year, Mr. Trump and Mr. Huang were talking often on the phone. When Marco Rubio, the president’s secretary of state and national security adviser, shared intelligence details about Mr. Huang’s romantic relationship with Alice Huang and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, Mr. Trump pooh-poohed it. Instead, he offered Mr. Huang a ride with him on Air Force One to meet with China’s president, Xi Jinping. The intelligence findings were eventually published by The Times, causing a cascade of revelations about Mr. Huang’s misbehaviors. Twelve days ago, Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted Mr. Huang’s resignation. But in the interim, the A.I. economy cratered, and when Mr. Trump pushed for him to be reinstated, the board unanimously voted to take him back.

到今年年初，特朗普和黄仁勋经常通电话。当国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥向他汇报了关于黄仁勋与黄乐的私情以及认为她是中国情报机构线人的细节时，特朗普不以为然。他反而邀请黄仁勋乘坐“空军一号”，随他一起会见中国国家主席习近平。《纽约时报》最终披露了这些情报调查结果，引发了一系列关于黄仁勋不当行为的爆料。12天前，英伟达董事会一致接受黄仁勋辞职。但在此期间，人工智能经济遭遇重挫，在特朗普力促黄仁勋复职后，董事会又一致投票同意让他回来。

Mr. Trump had reason to act: Nvidia’s plummeting stock price posed a threat to the global economy. When Nvidia underperforms, it drags the entire market down with it. By contrast, when Nvidia succeeds, it feeds a sprawling portfolio of data centers and developers. Mr. Huang is Nvidia; and Nvidia is A.I.; and A.I. is the American economy. To an extraordinary extent, the success of our stock market relies on this single man.

特朗普采取行动并非没有理由：英伟达股价暴跌对全球经济构成了威胁。英伟达表现不佳时，整个股市都会受到拖累。相反，英伟达的成功会带动庞大的数据中心和开发商群体。黄仁勋就是英伟达，英伟达就是人工智能，而人工智能就是美国经济。我们的股市能否繁荣，在很大程度上竟取决于这一个人。

I understand the board’s reasoning. It’s not the morality police. Its job is to make Nvidia’s stock price go up, and no one does that better than Mr. Huang. Several board members are themselves Nvidia billionaires, and some have been with Mr. Huang since Day 1. Also, what were they going to do — tell the president no?

我理解董事会的考量。它不是道德警察，它的职责是推动英伟达股价上涨，而在这方面，没有人比黄仁勋做得更好。几名董事会成员本身就是凭借英伟达股票跻身亿万富翁行列的，其中一些人从公司创立之初就追随黄仁勋。再说，他们又能怎么办呢——对总统说不吗？

And, it must be admitted, Mr. Huang truly is an irreplaceable businessman. He does the work of an entire C-suite. He is a manager, a thinker, a worker. He is a ruthless operations specialist, a customer relations whisperer, a talent scout and a strategic visionary. He can forecast the existence of new markets years in advance, and he can predict what the competitive dynamics of those markets will be once they come into being. In reporting on the growing humanoid robotics industry, I found that practically every such robot uses an Nvidia microchip for its brain — because Mr. Huang had directed Nvidia to start building these brains years before the robots existed.

而且，不得不承认，黄仁勋的确是一位无可替代的商界人士。他一个人就能承担整个高管团队的工作。他是管理者、思考者，也是实干家。他是无情的运营专家、深谙客户关系之道的高手、善于发掘人才的伯乐，以及富有远见的战略家。他能提前数年预见新市场的出现，还能预测这些市场形成后的竞争格局。在报道蓬勃发展的人形机器人产业时，我发现，几乎每一台此类机器人的大脑都采用了英伟达的微芯片——因为早在这些机器人问世之前，黄仁勋就已指示英伟达着手打造这些大脑。

Mr. Huang has many other talents. He is an accomplished public speaker — even though he has stage fright. He’s funny and charming and loves to tell jokes. He is an excellent draftsman and can draw, from memory, an elegant exploded diagram of one of his G.P.U.s. He can also label every part and tell you what it does, how much it costs and which of his Taiwanese suppliers he would pick up the phone to yell at if it were late. At 63, he retains a ton of energy and is surprisingly athletic. If Nvidia’s board had not rehired him, he could certainly have built a business to compete against the company.

黄仁勋还有许多其他才能。他是一位出色的演说家——尽管他也会怯场。他风趣迷人，喜欢讲笑话。他的制图功底十分出色，能凭记忆画出一张精美的英伟达图形处理器分解图。他还能标出每个零部件，告诉你它的用途、成本，如果该部件未能按时交货，他会打电话痛骂哪一家台湾供应商。63岁的他依然精力充沛，运动能力出奇地好。如果英伟达董事会没有重新聘用他，他完全有能力创办一家与英伟达竞争的企业。

In intervening to get Mr. Huang reinstated, Mr. Trump also played to the Main Street shareholder. Nvidia is one of the most popular stocks among retail investors, and its fame extends to unlikely places: While shooting clay pigeons in rural North Carolina earlier this year, I mentioned to a fellow shooter that I’d written a book about Nvidia. He pulled up his Robinhood account on his phone and walked me through his Nvidia trading history; then he yelled “pull” and nailed two targets in half a second. Such shareholders, I find, often have only a vague idea of what Nvidia makes. What they do know is that the stock should go up.

特朗普出面促成黄仁勋复职，也是在迎合普通股民。英伟达是散户投资者最青睐的股票之一，其知名度甚至超乎想象：今年早些时候，在北卡罗来纳州乡间打飞碟靶时，我向一位射击同伴提到自己写过一本关于英伟达的书。他立即在手机上打开自己的Robinhood账户，给我逐一介绍他买卖英伟达股票的记录；随后，他喊了一声“放靶”，半秒内就击中了两个目标。我发现，这类股东往往对英伟达究竟生产什么只有一个模糊的概念。但有一点他们很清楚：这只股票应该上涨。

But if Mr. Trump’s reinstatement is good for average investors, it is terrible for the rule of law. Nvidia may have broken the law and must be thoroughly investigated. In 2022, the Biden administration announced restrictions on sales to China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips. Nvidia responded by joining with new partners in Southeast Asia. These so-called cloud partners received preferential treatment when Nvidia was allocating its most advanced microchips, which, given the supply-demand imbalance for Nvidia equipment in late 2023, was sort of like the partners being handed a license to print money. The partners, mostly based in Singapore, were supposed to install the Nvidia-powered hardware they received in data centers in Malaysia. Instead, investigators say, some skirted the export ban by reselling the equipment to China.

然而，如果说特朗普促成黄仁勋复职有利于普通投资者，此举对法治而言则糟糕透顶。英伟达可能触犯了法律，必须受到彻底调查。2022年，拜登政府宣布限制英伟达最先进的芯片销往中国。作为回应，英伟达开始与东南亚的新合作伙伴开展业务。这些所谓的云服务合作伙伴在英伟达分配最先进的微芯片时享有优先待遇。鉴于2023年底英伟达的产品供不应求，这几乎等于给这些合作伙伴发了一张印钞许可证。这些合作伙伴大多位于新加坡，原本应将它们获得的搭载英伟达芯片的硬件设备安装到马来西亚的数据中心。然而，调查人员称，其中一些合作伙伴将设备转售给中国，绕过了出口禁令。

One cloud partner, Alan Wei Zhaolun, had accumulated enough money to buy a $40 million house. In February 2025, Mr. Zhaolun was arrested by the Singapore Police Force and accused of diverting his Nvidia chip allotment for resale to China. Singapore charged him with money laundering and fraud, and he could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. He has pleaded not guilty. (Nvidia says it stopped doing business with Mr. Zhaolun before his arrest.)

其中一家云服务合作伙伴的经营者韦兆伦积累的财富足以让他买下一栋价值4000万美元的豪宅。2025年2月，他被新加坡警方逮捕，被指将获配的英伟达芯片转售给中国。新加坡方面以洗钱和欺诈罪名对他提起指控，如果罪名成立，他可能面临最高20年的监禁。他表示不认罪。（英伟达表示在他被捕前已停止与他的业务往来。）

Alice Huang’s company was also a Nvidia cloud partner — and she was Jensen’s romantic partner, too. In June 2025, the Singapore Police questioned her and seized her passport. They returned it in February 2026 and later cited a lack of cooperation from the U.S. Department of Justice. Ms. Huang was banned from Singapore and now is reported to be in China. The U.S. intelligence community assessed her to be a Chinese intelligence asset whose company was suspected of diverting chips to China. (China denies this.)

黄乐的公司也是英伟达的云服务合作伙伴，而她本人是黄仁勋的情人。2025年6月，新加坡警方对她进行了问询，并扣押了她的护照。警方于2026年2月归还了她的护照，后来表示美国司法部不予配合。她已被禁止入境新加坡，据报道目前身在中国。美国情报界认定她是中国情报机构的线人，她的公司则涉嫌将芯片转运至中国。（中国否认这一点。）

I would like to know why Nvidia designated these two as preferred customers. I would like to know what suspicions Nvidia had about these and other Singapore-based businesses and what they did to respond. I would like to know why Nvidia changed its accounting procedures after sales in Singapore grew to 22 percent of its revenue. But I fear I may never get the complete answer.

我想知道为什么英伟达将这两个人指定为优先客户。我想知道英伟达对这些及其他新加坡企业存有哪些疑虑，又采取了什么应对措施。我还想知道，在新加坡的销售额增至公司营收的22%之后，英伟达为何改变了会计核算方式。但我担心，我可能永远得不到完整答案。

The U.S. Commerce Department, which was originally investigating alongside the Singapore Police Force, was transferred off the case after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, directly emailed investigators and name-checked their boss. The Justice Department took over — and this, Singapore authorities say, was when their investigation into Alice Huang stalled. President Trump, with his endorsement of Mr. Huang, has signaled to Nvidia’s board that the F.B.I. will not find anything too damaging. I wonder how hard it’s really looking.

美国商务部原本与新加坡警方共同展开调查，但在英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特直接给调查人员发送电子邮件，并特意提及他们的上司后，商务部被调离了此案的调查工作。司法部接手了调查——新加坡当局称，正是在这时，他们对黄乐的调查陷入停滞。特朗普对黄仁勋的支持向英伟达董事会释放出一个信号：联邦调查局不会查出任何对他过于不利的东西。我不禁怀疑，调查到底有多认真。

Mr. Huang’s reinstatement also sends a terrible signal regarding the fair treatment of women in the workplace. Mr. Huang had affairs with at least two subordinates: Kimberly Powell, a married health care executive at his company, and another woman, identified by Reuters, who remains anonymous. On Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Mr. Huang admitted to more affairs.

黄仁勋的复职也在职场女性能否受到公平对待的问题上释放了一个极其恶劣的信号。黄仁勋至少与两名下属有过婚外情：一名是已婚的医疗保健业务高管金伯莉·鲍威尔，另一名是路透社查明身份但未公开姓名的女性。周一，《华尔街日报》报道称，黄仁勋承认还有其他婚外情。

He will very likely face few repercussions for actions that would get anyone else in America fired. In fact, his romantic misadventures are being celebrated — on Monday, Mr. Trump posted a meme that riffed on the famous “Fight!” moment from his own assassination attempt, showing Mr. Huang with a bloody face and waving a red bra. The joke signals a return to “Mad Men” standards of behavior. The broader cultural implications for women are depressing to contemplate.

这些行为若发生在美国其他任何人身上都足以导致其被解雇，而他很可能几乎不用承担任何后果。事实上，他那些荒唐的情事甚至成了人们津津乐道的事情——周一，特朗普发布了一张网络恶搞图片，以自己遭遇暗杀未遂时那个著名的高喊“战斗！”的瞬间为蓝本，画面中黄仁勋满脸是血，挥舞着一件红色胸罩。这个玩笑表明，人们的行为准则正在倒退回《广告狂人》(Mad Men)所描绘的时代。这对女性来说意味着怎样一种更广泛的社会文化影响，想想就令人沮丧。

In an early draft of “The Thinking Machine,” my biography of Mr. Huang, I opined that he was one of the great men of history. I took that phrase out but I wish I’d left it in. Mr. Huang is as great as he is terrible.

在黄仁勋传记《思考机器》（The Thinking Machine，中译《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》）的早期草稿中，我曾写道，他是历史伟人之一。后来我删掉了这句话，但现在我希望自己当初没有这样做。黄仁勋有多伟大，就有多可怕。

He’s a titan of industry who reinvented the computer from the transistor up. He also betrayed his wife, his employees, his company and possibly his country. He’s a warm and charismatic jokester with a humble demeanor. He’s also a narcissist, an egomaniac and a manipulator — and when he gets in one of his moods, he behaves like a petty, insecure tyrant.

他是一位产业巨擘，从晶体管这一最基础的层面彻底重塑了计算机。但他也背叛了妻子、员工、公司，甚至可能背叛了自己的国家。他热情而富有魅力，爱开玩笑，举止谦和。但他同时也是一个自恋、自大、善于操纵他人的人——一旦脾气发作，他的表现就像一个心胸狭窄、缺乏安全感的暴君。

He’s a complicated figure, no question, and once the Democrats take office in January, they will go after him hard. But if I were on the board of Nvidia, and I were asking myself what to do, there’s also no question whom I’d choose.

毫无疑问，他是一个复杂的人物。等到明年1月民主党人掌权，他们必将对他穷追猛打。但如果我是英伟达董事会的一员，面对该如何抉择的问题，我会选择谁同样毫无疑问。

Welcome back, Mr. Huang. We hardly missed you.

欢迎回来，黄先生。我们还没来得及想念你呢。

Stephen Witt是黄仁勋传记《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》(The Thinking Machine)的作者。

blocks.text: STEPHEN WITT2026年11月25日
Jonathan Ernst/Reuters

When Jensen Huang returned to the floor of his Silicon Valley headquarters on Monday, his employees greeted him with a standing ovation. The rank and file of Nvidia love Mr. Huang, who has made many of them wealthy. In the midst of this celebration, I imagine his top executives must have exchanged a few glances. They know all about Mr. Huang’s abusive treatment of staff members, his extramarital relationships and Nvidia’s funny business in Southeast Asia. But, in the end, I’m sure they clapped, too.
周一，黄仁勋回到英伟达位于硅谷的总部时，员工们起立鼓掌欢迎。英伟达的普通员工都很爱戴黄仁勋，他让许多人赚得盆满钵满。在这欢庆的场面中，我想公司的高管们一定交换了几下眼神。他们对黄仁勋粗暴对待员工的行为、他的婚外情以及英伟达在东南亚那些见不得光的生意都心知肚明。不过，我相信最后他们也鼓掌了。

In the 11 days he was gone, Nvidia lost almost 30 percent of its value. Upon his return, Nvidia’s stock price recovered, adding almost a trillion dollars to the company’s market capitalization. They’re saying Jensen Huang is too big to fire. I say he’s the trillion-dollar man.
在他离开的11天里，英伟达市值损失近30%。他回归后，英伟达股价回升，公司市值增加近1万亿美元。人们说，黄仁勋重要到不能解雇。要我说，他是个价值万亿美元的男人。

Mr. Huang still has a number of looming scandals. Nvidia is being investigated by Congress, the Justice Department, the Securities and Exchange Commission and its own corporate board. The U.S. intelligence community seems to have compromising intelligence on Mr. Huang; he’s reportedly had numerous affairs, including one with a married corporate executive at his company and another with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
黄仁勋仍有多桩丑闻悬而未决。英伟达正受到国会、司法部、证券交易委员会及其自身董事会的调查。美国情报界似乎掌握了足以让黄仁勋陷入被动的情报；据报道，他有多次婚外情，包括与公司一名已婚女高管，以及与一名疑似中国间谍的女子。

Reporters have produced detailed accounts of his scathing encounters with staff members, which include bodily threats and ritual humiliation. He is scheduled to have a closed-door interview with House committees next Tuesday and to testify before the Senate two days later. For another corporate executive, any one of these scandals would be a career-killer. For Mr. Huang, it’s Monday morning.
记者们详细披露了他如何刻薄地对待员工，其中包括人身威胁和仪式化的羞辱。他定于下周二接受众议院多个委员会的闭门问询，并于两天后赴参议院作证。换作其他企业高管，这些丑闻中的任何一桩都足以断送职业生涯。对黄仁勋而言，这不过是一个寻常的周一早晨。

Mr. Huang’s invincibility derives from his close relationship with President Trump. Mr. Huang started cultivating this connection in 2025, when he and his wife, Lori, visited Mar-a-Lago. There, over dinner, he told Mr. Trump the compelling story of his rise from Denny’s waitstaff to semiconductor chief executive. In the course of writing Mr. Huang’s biography, I heard him tell this story many times. I never got tired of it — although I did notice the details change a bit at different tellings. The dazzled Mr. Trump fell hard for Mr. Huang. He also fell for Lori, whom on Monday he called a “fantastic woman” and “very supportive.”

黄仁勋之所以不可撼动，源于他与特朗普总统的密切关系。2025年，黄仁勋和妻子洛丽到访马阿拉歌庄园，从那时起，他便开始经营这段关系。席间，他向特朗普讲述了自己如何从连锁餐厅Denny's的一名服务员成长为半导体企业首席执行官的动人故事。在为黄仁勋撰写传记的过程中，我多次听他讲过这个故事，始终百听不厌——尽管我确实注意到，每次讲述的细节略有不同。听得入迷的特朗普彻底被黄仁勋征服了。他也很喜欢洛丽，周一还称她是个“了不起的女人”，对丈夫“非常支持”。

By the beginning of this year, Mr. Trump and Mr. Huang were talking often on the phone. When Marco Rubio, the president’s secretary of state and national security adviser, shared intelligence details about Mr. Huang’s romantic relationship with Alice Huang and the belief that she was a Chinese intelligence asset, Mr. Trump pooh-poohed it. Instead, he offered Mr. Huang a ride with him on Air Force One to meet with China’s president, Xi Jinping. The intelligence findings were eventually published by The Times, causing a cascade of revelations about Mr. Huang’s misbehaviors. Twelve days ago, Nvidia’s board unanimously accepted Mr. Huang’s resignation. But in the interim, the A.I. economy cratered, and when Mr. Trump pushed for him to be reinstated, the board unanimously voted to take him back.

到今年年初，特朗普和黄仁勋经常通电话。当国务卿兼国家安全顾问鲁比奥向他汇报了关于黄仁勋与黄乐的私情以及认为她是中国情报机构线人的细节时，特朗普不以为然。他反而邀请黄仁勋乘坐“空军一号”，随他一起会见中国国家主席习近平。《纽约时报》最终披露了这些情报调查结果，引发了一系列关于黄仁勋不当行为的爆料。12天前，英伟达董事会一致接受黄仁勋辞职。但在此期间，人工智能经济遭遇重挫，在特朗普力促黄仁勋复职后，董事会又一致投票同意让他回来。

Mr. Trump had reason to act: Nvidia’s plummeting stock price posed a threat to the global economy. When Nvidia underperforms, it drags the entire market down with it. By contrast, when Nvidia succeeds, it feeds a sprawling portfolio of data centers and developers. Mr. Huang is Nvidia; and Nvidia is A.I.; and A.I. is the American economy. To an extraordinary extent, the success of our stock market relies on this single man.
特朗普采取行动并非没有理由：英伟达股价暴跌对全球经济构成了威胁。英伟达表现不佳时，整个股市都会受到拖累。相反，英伟达的成功会带动庞大的数据中心和开发商群体。黄仁勋就是英伟达，英伟达就是人工智能，而人工智能就是美国经济。我们的股市能否繁荣，在很大程度上竟取决于这一个人。

I understand the board’s reasoning. It’s not the morality police. Its job is to make Nvidia’s stock price go up, and no one does that better than Mr. Huang. Several board members are themselves Nvidia billionaires, and some have been with Mr. Huang since Day 1. Also, what were they going to do — tell the president no?
我理解董事会的考量。它不是道德警察，它的职责是推动英伟达股价上涨，而在这方面，没有人比黄仁勋做得更好。几名董事会成员本身就是凭借英伟达股票跻身亿万富翁行列的，其中一些人从公司创立之初就追随黄仁勋。再说，他们又能怎么办呢——对总统说不吗？

And, it must be admitted, Mr. Huang truly is an irreplaceable businessman. He does the work of an entire C-suite. He is a manager, a thinker, a worker. He is a ruthless operations specialist, a customer relations whisperer, a talent scout and a strategic visionary. He can forecast the existence of new markets years in advance, and he can predict what the competitive dynamics of those markets will be once they come into being. In reporting on the growing humanoid robotics industry, I found that practically every such robot uses an Nvidia microchip for its brain — because Mr. Huang had directed Nvidia to start building these brains years before the robots existed.

而且，不得不承认，黄仁勋的确是一位无可替代的商界人士。他一个人就能承担整个高管团队的工作。他是管理者、思考者，也是实干家。他是无情的运营专家、深谙客户关系之道的高手、善于发掘人才的伯乐，以及富有远见的战略家。他能提前数年预见新市场的出现，还能预测这些市场形成后的竞争格局。在报道蓬勃发展的人形机器人产业时，我发现，几乎每一台此类机器人的大脑都采用了英伟达的微芯片——因为早在这些机器人问世之前，黄仁勋就已指示英伟达着手打造这些大脑。

Mr. Huang has many other talents. He is an accomplished public speaker — even though he has stage fright. He’s funny and charming and loves to tell jokes. He is an excellent draftsman and can draw, from memory, an elegant exploded diagram of one of his G.P.U.s. He can also label every part and tell you what it does, how much it costs and which of his Taiwanese suppliers he would pick up the phone to yell at if it were late. At 63, he retains a ton of energy and is surprisingly athletic. If Nvidia’s board had not rehired him, he could certainly have built a business to compete against the company.
黄仁勋还有许多其他才能。他是一位出色的演说家——尽管他也会怯场。他风趣迷人，喜欢讲笑话。他的制图功底十分出色，能凭记忆画出一张精美的英伟达图形处理器分解图。他还能标出每个零部件，告诉你它的用途、成本，如果该部件未能按时交货，他会打电话痛骂哪一家台湾供应商。63岁的他依然精力充沛，运动能力出奇地好。如果英伟达董事会没有重新聘用他，他完全有能力创办一家与英伟达竞争的企业。

In intervening to get Mr. Huang reinstated, Mr. Trump also played to the Main Street shareholder. Nvidia is one of the most popular stocks among retail investors, and its fame extends to unlikely places: While shooting clay pigeons in rural North Carolina earlier this year, I mentioned to a fellow shooter that I’d written a book about Nvidia. He pulled up his Robinhood account on his phone and walked me through his Nvidia trading history; then he yelled “pull” and nailed two targets in half a second. Such shareholders, I find, often have only a vague idea of what Nvidia makes. What they do know is that the stock should go up.

特朗普出面促成黄仁勋复职，也是在迎合普通股民。英伟达是散户投资者最青睐的股票之一，其知名度甚至超乎想象：今年早些时候，在北卡罗来纳州乡间打飞碟靶时，我向一位射击同伴提到自己写过一本关于英伟达的书。他立即在手机上打开自己的Robinhood账户，给我逐一介绍他买卖英伟达股票的记录；随后，他喊了一声“放靶”，半秒内就击中了两个目标。我发现，这类股东往往对英伟达究竟生产什么只有一个模糊的概念。但有一点他们很清楚：这只股票应该上涨。

But if Mr. Trump’s reinstatement is good for average investors, it is terrible for the rule of law. Nvidia may have broken the law and must be thoroughly investigated. In 2022, the Biden administration announced restrictions on sales to China of Nvidia’s most advanced chips. Nvidia responded by joining with new partners in Southeast Asia. These so-called cloud partners received preferential treatment when Nvidia was allocating its most advanced microchips, which, given the supply-demand imbalance for Nvidia equipment in late 2023, was sort of like the partners being handed a license to print money. The partners, mostly based in Singapore, were supposed to install the Nvidia-powered hardware they received in data centers in Malaysia. Instead, investigators say, some skirted the export ban by reselling the equipment to China.

然而，如果说特朗普促成黄仁勋复职有利于普通投资者，此举对法治而言则糟糕透顶。英伟达可能触犯了法律，必须受到彻底调查。2022年，拜登政府宣布限制英伟达最先进的芯片销往中国。作为回应，英伟达开始与东南亚的新合作伙伴开展业务。这些所谓的云服务合作伙伴在英伟达分配最先进的微芯片时享有优先待遇。鉴于2023年底英伟达的产品供不应求，这几乎等于给这些合作伙伴发了一张印钞许可证。这些合作伙伴大多位于新加坡，原本应将它们获得的搭载英伟达芯片的硬件设备安装到马来西亚的数据中心。然而，调查人员称，其中一些合作伙伴将设备转售给中国，绕过了出口禁令。

One cloud partner, Alan Wei Zhaolun, had accumulated enough money to buy a $40 million house. In February 2025, Mr. Zhaolun was arrested by the Singapore Police Force and accused of diverting his Nvidia chip allotment for resale to China. Singapore charged him with money laundering and fraud, and he could face up to 20 years in prison if convicted. He has pleaded not guilty. (Nvidia says it stopped doing business with Mr. Zhaolun before his arrest.)
其中一家云服务合作伙伴的经营者韦兆伦积累的财富足以让他买下一栋价值4000万美元的豪宅。2025年2月，他被新加坡警方逮捕，被指将获配的英伟达芯片转售给中国。新加坡方面以洗钱和欺诈罪名对他提起指控，如果罪名成立，他可能面临最高20年的监禁。他表示不认罪。（英伟达表示在他被捕前已停止与他的业务往来。）

Alice Huang’s company was also a Nvidia cloud partner — and she was Jensen’s romantic partner, too. In June 2025, the Singapore Police questioned her and seized her passport. They returned it in February 2026 and later cited a lack of cooperation from the U.S. Department of Justice. Ms. Huang was banned from Singapore and now is reported to be in China. The U.S. intelligence community assessed her to be a Chinese intelligence asset whose company was suspected of diverting chips to China. (China denies this.)
黄乐的公司也是英伟达的云服务合作伙伴，而她本人是黄仁勋的情人。2025年6月，新加坡警方对她进行了问询，并扣押了她的护照。警方于2026年2月归还了她的护照，后来表示美国司法部不予配合。她已被禁止入境新加坡，据报道目前身在中国。美国情报界认定她是中国情报机构的线人，她的公司则涉嫌将芯片转运至中国。（中国否认这一点。）

I would like to know why Nvidia designated these two as preferred customers. I would like to know what suspicions Nvidia had about these and other Singapore-based businesses and what they did to respond. I would like to know why Nvidia changed its accounting procedures after sales in Singapore grew to 22 percent of its revenue. But I fear I may never get the complete answer.
我想知道为什么英伟达将这两个人指定为优先客户。我想知道英伟达对这些及其他新加坡企业存有哪些疑虑，又采取了什么应对措施。我还想知道，在新加坡的销售额增至公司营收的22%之后，英伟达为何改变了会计核算方式。但我担心，我可能永远得不到完整答案。

The U.S. Commerce Department, which was originally investigating alongside the Singapore Police Force, was transferred off the case after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, directly emailed investigators and name-checked their boss. The Justice Department took over — and this, Singapore authorities say, was when their investigation into Alice Huang stalled. President Trump, with his endorsement of Mr. Huang, has signaled to Nvidia’s board that the F.B.I. will not find anything too damaging. I wonder how hard it’s really looking.
美国商务部原本与新加坡警方共同展开调查，但在英伟达总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特直接给调查人员发送电子邮件，并特意提及他们的上司后，商务部被调离了此案的调查工作。司法部接手了调查——新加坡当局称，正是在这时，他们对黄乐的调查陷入停滞。特朗普对黄仁勋的支持向英伟达董事会释放出一个信号：联邦调查局不会查出任何对他过于不利的东西。我不禁怀疑，调查到底有多认真。

Mr. Huang’s reinstatement also sends a terrible signal regarding the fair treatment of women in the workplace. Mr. Huang had affairs with at least two subordinates: Kimberly Powell, a married health care executive at his company, and another woman, identified by Reuters, who remains anonymous. On Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Mr. Huang admitted to more affairs.
黄仁勋的复职也在职场女性能否受到公平对待的问题上释放了一个极其恶劣的信号。黄仁勋至少与两名下属有过婚外情：一名是已婚的医疗保健业务高管金伯莉·鲍威尔，另一名是路透社查明身份但未公开姓名的女性。周一，《华尔街日报》报道称，黄仁勋承认还有其他婚外情。

He will very likely face few repercussions for actions that would get anyone else in America fired. In fact, his romantic misadventures are being celebrated — on Monday, Mr. Trump posted a meme that riffed on the famous “Fight!” moment from his own assassination attempt, showing Mr. Huang with a bloody face and waving a red bra. The joke signals a return to “Mad Men” standards of behavior. The broader cultural implications for women are depressing to contemplate.

这些行为若发生在美国其他任何人身上都足以导致其被解雇，而他很可能几乎不用承担任何后果。事实上，他那些荒唐的情事甚至成了人们津津乐道的事情——周一，特朗普发布了一张网络恶搞图片，以自己遭遇暗杀未遂时那个著名的高喊“战斗！”的瞬间为蓝本，画面中黄仁勋满脸是血，挥舞着一件红色胸罩。这个玩笑表明，人们的行为准则正在倒退回《广告狂人》(Mad Men)所描绘的时代。这对女性来说意味着怎样一种更广泛的社会文化影响，想想就令人沮丧。

In an early draft of “The Thinking Machine,” my biography of Mr. Huang, I opined that he was one of the great men of history. I took that phrase out but I wish I’d left it in. Mr. Huang is as great as he is terrible.
在黄仁勋传记《思考机器》（The Thinking Machine，中译《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》）的早期草稿中，我曾写道，他是历史伟人之一。后来我删掉了这句话，但现在我希望自己当初没有这样做。黄仁勋有多伟大，就有多可怕。

He’s a titan of industry who reinvented the computer from the transistor up. He also betrayed his wife, his employees, his company and possibly his country. He’s a warm and charismatic jokester with a humble demeanor. He’s also a narcissist, an egomaniac and a manipulator — and when he gets in one of his moods, he behaves like a petty, insecure tyrant.
他是一位产业巨擘，从晶体管这一最基础的层面彻底重塑了计算机。但他也背叛了妻子、员工、公司，甚至可能背叛了自己的国家。他热情而富有魅力，爱开玩笑，举止谦和。但他同时也是一个自恋、自大、善于操纵他人的人——一旦脾气发作，他的表现就像一个心胸狭窄、缺乏安全感的暴君。

He’s a complicated figure, no question, and once the Democrats take office in January, they will go after him hard. But if I were on the board of Nvidia, and I were asking myself what to do, there’s also no question whom I’d choose.
毫无疑问，他是一个复杂的人物。等到明年1月民主党人掌权，他们必将对他穷追猛打。但如果我是英伟达董事会的一员，面对该如何抉择的问题，我会选择谁同样毫无疑问。
Welcome back, Mr. Huang. We hardly missed you.
欢迎回来，黄先生。我们还没来得及想念你呢。
Stephen Witt是黄仁勋传记《黄仁勋：英伟达之芯》(The Thinking Machine)的作者。
翻译：纽约时报中文网

items.body:
小米汽车 Q1 亏损 31 亿、Q2 亏损 26 亿、Q3 亏损 34 亿，手机均价暴涨40%

“我们连续两个季度营收站稳了千亿，并且收入的同比下滑的幅度在逐步的收窄。”11月24日晚，小米集团总裁卢伟冰在三季度业绩媒体电话会上如是说。

财报显示，今年一季度，小米集团营收同比下降10.9%。到了二季度，营收回到千亿元以上，达到1089.22亿元，同比降幅收窄至6.1%。三季度，小米实现营收1072.4亿元，同比降幅收窄至5.2%。

收入降幅逐季收窄，经调整净利润的降幅却从二季度的42.6%扩大至三季度的56.8%。7月至9月，小米经调整净利润从去年同期的113.11亿元降至48.84亿元，一个季度少了64.27亿元。

从毛利看，缺口主要集中在手机和创新业务。三季度，小米集团毛利同比减少43.2亿元，其中手机业务减少9.1亿元，新能源汽车及AI等创新业务减少约28亿元。同期，集团营业费用同比增长1.4%，补贴收入减少，也使其他收入从去年同期的约17亿元降至约6亿元。

“三季度的智能手机行业，可能是从业以来我感觉最难的一个季度。”小米集团总裁卢伟冰在当晚的业绩会上说。三个月前的二季度业绩会上，他曾预计下半年内存涨价会放缓，当时他对下半年小米手机业务的毛利率仍有信心，认为“最困难的阶段已经看到尾声”。

此次，卢伟冰表示，内存涨幅确实收窄了，但价格仍处高位，小米接下来要靠产品创新和调整机型结构来消化成本、稳住毛利率。三季度，小米主动减少了低端机出货；9月发布的旗舰机小米18 Pro起售价为5999元，也比上一代同为12GB+256GB的版本贵了1000元。

随着低端机出货减少、中国大陆市场在全球出货中的比重上升，小米手机全球平均售价同比上涨39.8%至1486元，创下历史新高。尽管出货量同比下降29.1%至3070万部，手机业务收入仍达455.8亿元，较去年同期的459.7亿元仅降0.8%。

值得注意的是，虽然均价上涨稳住了收入，核心零部件涨价仍在挤压小米手机业务的毛利。财报显示，三季度小米手机业务销售成本同比增长1.3%。手机毛利率从二季度的8.5%回升至9.2%，仍低于去年同期的11.1%，毛利也从去年同期的51.0亿元降至41.8亿元。

小米的出货量降幅也超过了行业整体。Omdia数据显示，三季度全球智能手机出货量同比下降20%，小米下降29.1%，其中在中国和印度分别下降20%和28%。小米虽仍居全球第三，市场份额也连续三个季度环比回升至12.1%，但还是低于去年同期的13.6%。

IoT与生活消费产品同样受到零部件涨价影响，但收入降幅收窄得更快。一、二季度，这项业务收入分别同比下降23.7%和19.2%，三季度收入为271.5亿元，同比仅降1.4%。小米在财报中解释，部分生活消费产品收入仍在下滑，但笔记本电脑、智能大家电和海外平板业务的收入增长抵消了部分降幅。

同期，互联网服务收入为94.5亿元，其中约74亿元来自广告。虽然这项业务的收入不到手机业务的四分之一，但销售成本仅为24.8亿元，毛利率达73.8%，贡献毛利69.7亿元，比手机业务多出近28亿元。

更大的毛利缺口来自新能源汽车及AI等创新业务。三季度，小米汽车收入同比下降19.9%至227亿元，主要受交付量减少、售价较高的SU7 Ultra交付占比下降影响。整个分部去年同期尚有7亿元经营收益，今年二季度已出现26亿元经营亏损，三季度亏损进一步扩大至34亿元。

进入四季度，9月上市的增程车型澎程N70、N90开始放量，小米汽车10月单月交付量创下年内新高。卢伟冰在业绩会上表示，他对11月、12月的交付有信心，但存储和部分大宗商品涨价仍会推高整车成本，小米希望通过扩大交付规模、提高运营效率来消化部分压力。

对于汽车业务何时能恢复盈亏平衡，卢伟冰没有给出具体时间。他解释，汽车、AI和芯片业务都计入这一分部，“这个季度亏损扩大的核心原因，还是我们大幅增加了AI的投入”。

今年前三季度，小米集团研发开支为274亿元，同比增长16.5%。小米集团副总裁兼首席财务官林世伟在业绩会上透露，其中与AI相关的研发费用占比超过三成，年初定下的全年约160亿元AI投入计划仍在推进。

9月，小米开源了MiMo-V2.6系列模型，Pro版每百万个Token定价未命中缓存的输入收费3元，输出收费6元，Flash版对应为1元和2元。开发者可通过小米MiMo开放平台调用模型，用户也可通过第三方AI办公产品使用Pro版。

林世伟在业绩会上透露，MiMo的API调用量和小米的AI相关收入都在增加，但谈到这项业务目前的阶段，他表示，“现在还是一个非常大规模的投入期”。

小米尚未单独披露AI相关收入。三季报中，创新业务分部的“其他相关业务”收入同比增长68.9%至约12亿元，其中还包括汽车售后服务收入。

谈及未来几个季度，卢伟冰认为，内存成本高企、国内需求不足和行业竞争加剧等经营压力仍然存在。

小米把部分增长希望放在了海外。三季度，“手机×AIoT”分部的海外收入占比已达49.1%，同比、环比均有提升。接下来，小米计划扩大米家产品在欧洲的销售，汽车业务也计划于2027年第三季度率先进入德国市场。

卢伟冰说，在内需不足的环境下，海外市场对小米集团能够起到“稳定器和助推器的作用”。

items.summary: 从兵工厂小镇到英伟达核心圈：黄乐的人生轨迹与间谍疑云 Telegraph | 原文链接 | 频道大全
items.body:
孟建国, KEITH BRADSHER, 马语琴, 傅才德, ANA SWANSON2026年11月25日

The rows of matching yellow apartment blocks are each four stories tall and bear a name from another era: Patriotic Village No. 5.

一排排样式一致的黄色公寓楼，都是四层高，带着一个属于另一个时代的名字：爱国五村。

One of the weathered apartments belonged to the family of Alice Huang, whose father worked as a clerk at a sprawling complex of weapons factories in Nanzhushan, a village nestled in the hills of southern China’s Hunan Province.

其中一套略显斑驳的公寓曾属于黄乐(Alice Huang)的家庭，她的父亲曾在中国南部湖南省群山环抱的楠竹山镇一座庞大的兵工厂园区内当文员。

The complex had a number too: State-Owned Factory No. 282. It made everything from hand grenades to parts for guided missiles, and under China’s Soviet-style planned economy, life in the area revolved around it.

这座工厂综合体也有一个编号：国营282厂。它生产从手榴弹到制导导弹零部件的各类产品，在中国的苏式计划经济体制下，当地的生活都围绕着这座工厂运转。

Today, the town is well past its prime. The factory complex remains, but after state-owned enterprise layoffs, many young people started moving away. By the mid-2000s, one of them was Ms. Huang, who rose from this fading industrial town to the inner circle of the man behind America’s artificial intelligence boom — and into the middle of a geopolitical crisis.

如今，这座小镇早已风光不再。厂区依然存在，但在国有企业下岗潮之后，许多年轻人开始外迁。到2000年代中期，黄乐也成为其中之一，她从这座日渐衰落的工业小镇一路崛起，进入美国人工智能热潮推动者的核心圈子——并卷入了一场地缘政治危机的中心。

The New York Times traced Ms. Huang’s life through visits to Nanzhushan village and four countries, drawing on internal company documents, corporate filings and interviews with more than a dozen people familiar with her. Ms. Huang has not responded to requests for comment.

《纽约时报》通过走访楠竹山镇和四个国家，结合公司内部文件、企业备案资料以及对十余名熟悉她的人士的采访，追踪了黄乐的人生轨迹。黄乐未回应置评请求。

The reporting reveals previously unreported details of her upbringing, education and business dealings that show how Ms. Huang’s life has been intertwined with China’s military-industrial complex since childhood.

此次报道披露了她此前未曾公开的成长背景、教育经历和商业往来细节，揭示了她的人生自童年起便与中国军工复合体紧密交织。

U.S. intelligence officials believe Ms. Huang was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 through this year. That period overlapped with at least part of the time she allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, the chief executive of American chip giant Nvidia. It also coincided with large purchases of Nvidia’s advanced chips by her company Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence agencies have also gathered evidence that her business partner, Kang Wei, who was often introduced as her husband, worked with the same Chinese spy agency.

美国情报官员认为，从2025年春季到今年，黄乐一直与中国国家安全部的一名官员保持联系。这一时期与据称她和美国芯片巨头英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋保持婚外情的时间至少有部分重叠，也与她的Megaspeed公司大量采购英伟达先进芯片的时间相吻合。美国情报机构还收集了证据，表明她经常对外介绍为丈夫的商业伙伴康伟也与同一家中国情报机构有合作。

Those contacts led some U.S. officials to suspect that Mr. Huang, who resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive on Nov. 12, had been targeted in a Chinese intelligence operation, which Beijing denies. The case heightened concerns in Washington about Beijing’s efforts to acquire advanced American chips and accelerate its A.I. ambitions.

这些接触让一些美国官员怀疑，已于11月12日辞去英伟达首席执行官职务的黄仁勋曾是中国情报行动的目标，北京方面对此予以否认。这一案件加剧了华盛顿对北京试图获取美国先进芯片并加速其人工智能雄心的担忧。

The claims about Ms. Huang continue to reverberate. On Monday, in a stunning turnabout, Nvidia’s board of directors reinstated Mr. Huang as C.E.O. after pressure from President Trump. Despite the president’s support, Mr. Huang and his ties to Ms. Huang are expected to be scrutinized in Congress next week, when he is set to appear before three committees.

围绕黄乐的指控仍在持续发酵。周一发生了一场令人震惊的逆转，英伟达董事会在特朗普总统施压后恢复了黄仁勋的首席执行官职务。尽管有总统支持，黄仁勋及其与黄乐的关系预计仍将在下周受到国会审查，届时他将出席三个委员会的听证会。

在这些“爱国五村”小区的四层楼房中，有一套公寓曾属于黄乐的家庭。

Raised in a Weapons Town

兵工厂小镇的童年

Since childhood, her life was surrounded by China’s defense establishment. She attended a school for children of workers at a weapons factory owned by a state-run company repeatedly sanctioned by the U.S. government.

自儿时起，她的生活便被中国的国防体系所包围。她就读的是一所子弟学校，其中的学生是一家国有企业旗下的兵工厂职工子女，该企业曾屡次遭到美国政府制裁。

Ms. Huang had established her own ties to the Chinese government by the time she was an adult. She worked briefly for China’s state broadcaster and later made an investment that would connect her to the son of a former Chinese vice premier. As an entrepreneur, she remained within the state’s orbit, securing backing and funding from local government officials for a business that served Beijing’s strategic imperatives.

到成年时，黄乐已建立了自己与中国政府的联系。她曾在中国官方广播电视机构短暂工作，后来进行的一项投资使她与一位中国前副总理之子产生了交集。作为一名企业家，她始终处于体制的轨道之内，为一项服务于北京战略要务的业务赢得了地方政府官员的支持和资金。

Through a web of family and business relationships that gave her access to Nvidia chips, she is linked to Chinese state-owned defense contractors that supply the People’s Liberation Army.

通过一张让她得以获取英伟达芯片的家庭和商业关系网，她与为中国人民解放军供货的中国国有国防承包商保持了关联。

一座兵工厂综合体曾是楠竹山镇的主要雇主。其中一栋建筑上的红色横幅写着：“军民团结一家亲”。

The story of a factory worker’s daughter from rural China who found herself at the center of a global struggle over technology and espionage is one of ambition, reinvention and China’s rise from a drab socialist state to a shiny world power.

一个出身于中国乡间工厂的工人家庭之女发现自己进入了全球技术与间谍之争的中心——这是一个关于野心、自我重塑，以及中国从了无生气的社会主义国家崛起为光鲜世界大国的故事。

Alice Huang grew up in the shadow of Mao Zedong, whose birthplace is just a 20-minute drive away. Her father worked at the local plant, part of Jiangnan Industries Group, a subsidiary of the military supplier Norinco.

黄乐从小在毛泽东的影响下长大，他的出生地离她家仅20分钟车程。她的父亲在当地工厂工作，该厂隶属于军工供应商中国兵器工业集团旗下的江南工业集团。

She attended local schools, where she was a good student but not at the top of her class, according to the neighborhood committee cadre. She later enrolled in a nursing school in the nearby city of Xiangtan, according to a current student named Joanna, who said a teacher had described Alice Huang as a graduate.

据居委会干部介绍，她在当地学校就读，成绩不错，但并非名列前茅。她后来就读于邻近湘潭市的一所护理学校，据一名名叫乔安娜的在校学生说，一位老师曾提到黄乐是该校毕业生。

After graduating, Ms. Huang, who turns 44 next month, did what tens of millions of Chinese in her generation did. She left small-town life for better opportunities in bigger cities like Beijing and Shanghai.

毕业后，下个月将满44岁的黄乐做了她那一代数千万中国人都在做的事：离开小镇生活，前往北京、上海等大城市寻找更好的机会。

Over two decades, she became a globe-trotting executive overseeing Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia’s advanced chips.

20多年来，她成长为一名奔走于世界各地的高管，执掌着总部位于新加坡的Megaspeed公司，该公司采购了价值数十亿美元的英伟达先进芯片。

Yet traces of her early life proved difficult to pin down. Villagers gossiped about the family, whom some remembered, but none could identify the precise house where she grew up. Local officials disagreed about her mother’s background.

然而，她早年生活的痕迹却难以捉摸。村民们对这家人议论纷纷，有些人还记得他们，但没人能指出她家的屋宅在哪。地方官员对她母亲的背景也说法不一。

Two Times journalists interviewed village leaders and several residents before the police halted their reporting and took them to the nearest police station for questioning.

时报的两名记者采访了村干部和几位村民，随后警方叫停了他们的采访，并将他们带到最近的派出所问话。

黄乐的父亲曾在该兵工厂担任文员，她就读于楠竹山镇一所为该厂职工子女开设的学校。

By her 20s, Alice Huang had left Nanzhushan. She worked for state television at the flagship channel of China’s state broadcaster, according to an online résumé and a former classmate.

20多岁时，黄乐已离开楠竹山镇。根据一份在线简历和一位前同学的说法，她曾在中国国家广播电视机构的旗舰频道工作。

She attended Hong Kong Baptist University in 2006 to pursue a master’s degree in media management. The program was new and drew many students from mainland China, who, one former professor recalled, were often there for reasons beyond education. Hong Kong was a gateway to the world, with open internet and easy travel.

2006年，她进入香港浸会大学攻读传媒管理硕士学位。该课程当时刚刚开设，吸引了许多来自中国内地的学生，一位前教授回忆说，他们来这里往往有着教育以外的目的。香港当时是通往世界的门户，拥有开放的互联网和便利的出行条件。

A classmate said she often wore designer brands, a contrast with the jeans and T-shirts most other students wore. She often skipped classes, the person said, and many students suspected that connections in China kept her in the school.

一位同学表示，她经常穿名牌服装，与大多数穿牛仔裤和T恤的学生形成鲜明对比。这名人士还说，她经常旷课，许多学生怀疑她在内地的关系网保住了她的学籍。

In 2010, she and her older sister, Huang Yu, registered a company at the address of a building inside a members-only golf course in Beijing. Their father, Huang Guobin, by then of retirement age, was listed as a company supervisor in Chinese corporate records.

2010年，她和姐姐黄瑜用北京一家会员制高尔夫球场内一座建筑的地址注册了一家公司。中国企业工商记录显示，当时已到退休年龄的父亲黄国斌被列为公司监事。

The golf course was a magnet for government officials and the businessmen who courted them. Its restaurant served shark fin, and its chef had worked at the walled compound where Chinese leaders host heads of state, according to Chinese media reports. A senior civil-aviation official was once punished for accepting more than 50 free rounds of golf there.

这家高尔夫球场是政府官员和巴结他们的商人的聚集地。据中国媒体报道，其餐厅供应鱼翅，厨师曾在中国领导人接待外国元首的国宾馆工作。一名民航系统高级官员曾因在该球场接受超过50次免费高尔夫球服务而受到处分。

It is unclear what the Huang family business did. It reported taking in only about $4,500 in 2012. In 2014, Alice transferred her stake to her sister.

目前尚不清楚黄家这家公司的具体业务。该公司申报2012年的收入仅约4500美元。2014年，黄乐将自己的股份转让给了姐姐。

Soon, the Huang sisters moved on to far larger ventures.

不久，黄氏姐妹便转向了规模大得多的商业项目。

The Data Center Highway

数据中心高速公路

Alice Huang’s hometown Nanzhushan sits next to the G60 expressway. Follow it some 700 miles to the northeast and it ends in Shanghai, passing in its final miles by a cluster of giant data centers in the city’s Songjiang District.

黄乐的家乡楠竹山镇紧邻G60高速公路。沿这条公路向东北方向行驶约1200公里，终点便是上海，并且在最后的路段经过该市松江区的一处大型数据中心集群。

There, she made her mark with a sprawling data center featuring advanced American A.I. chips. The project also brought her into the orbit of Nvidia’s Mr. Huang.

在那里，她凭借一座配备美国先进人工智能芯片的大型数据中心崭露头角。该项目也将她带入了英伟达的黄仁勋的社交圈。

Alice Huang was in Shanghai by the mid-2010s. In meetings, she introduced a well-known financier, Kang Wei, as her husband. Together, they invested in a network of companies with overlapping ownership, shareholders and contact information, according to corporate filings and records from WireScreen, a data platform.

到2000年代中期，黄乐已身处上海。在商务会面中，她将知名金融家康伟介绍为自己的丈夫。企业备案资料和数据平台WireScreen的记录显示，两人共同投资了一系列在所有权、股东和联系信息上存在重叠的公司。

She put her money alongside some of China’s most sophisticated and politically connected financiers. At one point, she used a Caribbean shell company to invest in a Chinese medical device maker before its public share sale, according to a filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Among the other investors was a fund founded by the son of Liu He, who was then a vice premier of China and a member of the Communist Party’s ruling Politburo.

她与一些中国最精明、政治人脉最广的金融家共同出资。根据提交给香港交易所的一份文件，她曾通过一家加勒比空壳公司在一家中国医疗器械制造商公开募股前对其进行投资。其他投资者中包括时任中国副总理、中共中央政治局委员的刘鹤的儿子所创立的一只基金。

黄乐和康伟参与开发了这座位于上海西郊的数据中心。场地周围的围墙顶部装有电网。

Alice Huang initially owned a key holding company for the network. In 2017, as with the golf company, she transferred her stake to her older sister.

黄乐最初拥有该商业网络一家核心控股公司的股权。2017年，与高尔夫公司如出一辙，她将股份转让给了姐姐。

During Covid, Alice Huang and Mr. Kang helped develop a data center with local government support — a project that made her a potentially useful contact for State Security. When it was finished, the project, called the Yangtze River Delta A.I. Advanced Computing Center, featured Nvidia chips and leased computing power to companies.

新冠疫情期间，黄乐和康伟在地方政府支持下参与开发了一座数据中心——这一项目使她成为国家安全部门眼中有潜在利用价值的联络对象。该项目名为长三角人工智能超算中心，建成后配备了英伟达芯片，并向企业出租算力。

The data center and a company set up to acquire Nvidia servers and rent out computing power, called Century Litong, soon became a key link in a chip supply pipeline. The flows traveled into a network of companies linked to Chinese military contractors like the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, China’s state aerospace and defense conglomerate, and an A.I. lab linked to the People’s Liberation Army.

这座数据中心以及一家为采购英伟达服务器并出租算力而成立的名为世纪利通的公司很快成为芯片供应渠道中的关键一环。这些芯片流向了一个企业网络，其中包括中国国有航空航天与国防企业集团中国航空工业集团等中国军工承包商，以及一家与中国人民解放军有关联的人工智能实验室。

As borders reopened after the pandemic, the couple looked abroad. In 2022, Nvidia’s sales team had introduced Alice Huang to the Chinese technology giant Alibaba. She and Mr. Kang began pitching investors on a venture to buy Nvidia chips, install them in Southeast Asia and sell the A.I. computing power to Chinese companies.

随着疫情后跨境往来恢复，这对伴侣将目光投向了海外。2022年，英伟达的销售团队将黄乐介绍给了中国科技巨头阿里巴巴。她和康伟开始向投资者推介一个项目，计划购买英伟达芯片并部署在东南亚，再向中国企业出售人工智能算力。

Megaspeed位于新加坡的办公室。该公司采购了价值数十亿美元的英伟达先进人工智能芯片。

In 2023, Alice Huang used a British Virgin Islands company to buy a Singaporean subsidiary of 7Road, a gaming company. It became Megaspeed.

2023年，黄乐通过一家英属维尔京群岛公司收购了游戏公司第七大道旗下的一家新加坡子公司。该公司随后更名为Megaspeed。

The U.S. government had begun tightening restrictions on sales of advanced A.I. chips to China, prompting companies to eliminate ties to the mainland. Alice Huang began cultivating an image as an international executive. She posted pictures of herself drinking wine at fine restaurants across Asia alongside Nvidia’s Mr. Huang and tycoons from the region’s chip and electronics supply chain.

美国政府当时已开始收紧对华销售先进人工智能芯片的限制，促使相关企业切断与中国大陆的联系。黄乐开始塑造自己作为国际化高管的形象。她在社交媒体上发布自己在亚洲各地高档餐厅饮酒的照片，身旁正是英伟达的黄仁勋以及该地区芯片和电子供应链的商界大亨。

To those around them, their China connections were obvious. In one pitch deck from 2025, their data center business heralded computing centers operating in Shanghai, Shenzhen, Anhui, Sichuan, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia — a mix of locations that tied a data center network in China to one in Southeast Asia, where the most advanced Nvidia chips could be bought.

对周围的人而言，他们与中国的联系显而易见。在2025年的一份融资推介演示文稿中，他们的数据中心业务宣传了在上海、深圳、安徽、四川以及马来西亚、泰国和印度尼西亚运营的计算中心——这种布局将中国境内的数据中心网络与东南亚网络联系在一起，而在东南亚可以买到最先进的英伟达芯片。

Although the relationship with Mr. Huang was not yet public, U.S. intelligence agencies had identified Alice Huang as an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. By the fall of 2025, President Trump had been briefed on the intelligence.

尽管她与黄仁勋的关系当时尚未公开，但美国情报机构已认定黄乐为中国国家安全部的线人。到2025年秋季，特朗普总统已听取了有关该情报的简报。

2024年6月，黄仁勋与黄乐相邻而坐，摄于台湾台北。

‘We Are All Gossiping.’

“大家都在议论这件事。”

Alice Huang’s newfound prominence has reached Nanzhushan.

黄乐新近获得的知名度已经传到了楠竹山镇。

One store manager said locals had been discussing the news quietly. Although coverage has not been widely censored, the subject remains sensitive.

一家商店经理表示，当地人一直在私下议论这一消息。尽管相关报道尚未遭到大范围审查，但这一话题依然敏感。

In Patriotic Village No. 5, people were less cautious.

在爱国五村，人们的顾忌则少得多。

“We are all gossiping about it,” admitted a neighbor surnamed Zheng, who once made hand grenades at the factory. Another resident said many had been discussing her looks.

“大家都在议论这件事，”一位曾在厂里制造手榴弹的郑姓邻居坦言。另一位居民说，很多人一直在讨论她的长相。

In nearby Xiangtan, a man surnamed Han said he looked up to Alice Huang. Times have been tough, and it was becoming harder for local people to make money, he said. That a homegrown person could get rich was impressive.

在邻近的湘潭，一位姓韩的男子表示他很钦佩黄乐。他说，如今世道艰难，当地人赚钱越来越不容易，一个本土出身的人能够发家致富，令人印象深刻。

“I don’t care if she is the mistress of Jensen Huang,” he said. “She is great because she is a successful businesswoman.”

“我不在乎她是不是黄仁勋的情妇，”他说。“我觉得她挺厉害的，因为她是一个成功的生意人。”

艾莎(Alexandra Stevenson)、Selam Gebrekidan、 Murphy Zhao和Anjali Tsui自香港、Xinyun Wu和Pei-Lin Wu自台湾台北对本文有报道贡献。Ruoxin Zhang对本文有研究贡献。

孟建国(Paul Mozur)是时报全球科技记者，常驻台北。此前，他自香港、上海和首尔报道亚洲科技与政治的交叉议题。

Keith Bradsher是《纽约时报》北京分社社长，此前曾任上海分社社长、香港分社社长、底特律分社社长，以及华盛顿记者。他在新冠疫情期间常驻中国进行报道。

Mara Hvistendahl是国际新闻版块调查记者，可以通过电邮mara.hvistendahl@nytimes.com与她联系。

傅才德(Michael Forsythe)是《纽约时报》调查记者，常驻纽约。他此前曾驻中国，广泛报道该国各类议题。

Ana Swanson报道贸易和国际经济新闻，常驻华盛顿。她从事新闻工作已超过十年。

翻译：纽约时报中文网
